New refs: `docs/release-engineering.md`, `docs/config-layering.md`.

## Session Briefing Card

`~/obsidian/dream-memory/memory/profile/00-pi-active-context.md` — compact (≤1500 tok) briefing card injected on every session start via dream-memory harness. Covers: claude-bridge provider config, active projects, pi extensions, openclaw separation, active-memory/dreaming behaviour.

- Named `00-` → loads first in lex-sort, guaranteed within the 8-file cap.
- Keep under 6 kB. Update when project focus or runtime config changes.
- Do not add timestamps or session-specific content (breaks LLM cache).
- Format: stable markdown tables and bullets — no counters, no dates.

## Pi Context Block (session-start memory)

`~/obsidian/dream-memory/memory/profile/MEMORY.md` is the single file auto-injected every session (≤1500 tokens, cache-stable). It contains:
- **Preferences & Policies** (refs to detail files)
- **Infrastructure** notes
- **Pi Stack** — fork, extensions, packages, claude-bridge, active-memory, dream
- **Active Projects & OpenClaw** — high-traffic repos + openclaw env separation

Dream upserts individual H2 sections when relevant events accumulate. Manual updates are fine; keep the file under ~5.8 kB to stay within the token budget. Regenerate the Active Projects section when the project mix shifts significantly.

## pi-memory extraction

Per-turn `turn_end` extraction (CC `extractMemories` parity); consolidation cadence belongs to dream-memory. Before touching extraction gating, env vars, or the dream boundary, read `docs/memory-extraction-parity.md`.

## Pi Change Workflow

Use this before modifying `my-pi` or `pi-mono-fork`:

1. Read the local Pi docs above for the touched surface.
2. Choose extension/package first; if core is unavoidable, climb the extensibility ladder (existing hook/filter → new upstreamable hook/filter → inline patch as last resort) and write a short note justifying the chosen rung.

5. Make one incremental simplification when it is local, safe, and directly adjacent to the change.
6. Update `docs/pi-setup/catalog/*.yaml` and governed docs for setup/runtime changes; never hand-edit `docs/pi-setup/generated/`.

## Subagent routing

## Cache Stability (mandatory for fork + extension work)

Any change touching `forkAgent`, child agents, system-prompt construction, or background extractors **must** review the `pi-cache-stability` skill first. Anthropic prompt cache only helps when the prefix is byte-identical and alive within TTL — pi forks and extensions break this constantly without realising. The skill captures the L1/L2/L3 levers (`context: "slim"|"none"`, `systemPrompt` override, `BRIDGE_CACHE_TTL=1h`), the audit checklist, and the verification recipe. Source-of-truth doc: `docs/cache-strategy.md`.

## Pre-PR local review

**PR gate (run order):** `codex-review` → `code-craft-pr` → `matt-pocock/improve-codebase-architecture` → `docs-freshness-pr` (wire through `pr-pipeline-orchestrator`); resolve all Tier 1/2 findings and file Tier 3 as GitHub issues. This gate is the `.github/pull_request_template.md` checklist in both `my-pi` and `pi-mono-fork`.

Before opening/updating/declaring a PR ready, read `docs/review-guidelines.md` for the review lenses, P1 flag list, agent-ci command, and the ClawSweeper autonomous lane. Stop before PR on a real P1 — fix it or document the deferral.

## Verification

Before changing runtime extension behavior, run the relevant eval or add one if none exists.

- When installing, adding, modifying, or removing Pi extensions/packages, run the my-pi extension checks and the fork cache gate together:
  - `npm run test:extension-gate` (profile cache contracts, prompt-health fixtures, claude-bridge/dream-memory cache, skill/tool search, native aliases, Agent view, task tools) plus the individual `test:*:smoke`/`test:*:cache` scripts in `package.json` when touching one surface.

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Build all local pi extensions to pre-compiled .js/.mjs bundles.
#
# Strategy:
#   - Extensions that only import from node:* → compile .ts → .js (native import, no jiti)
#   - Extensions with pi-package imports (pi-coding-agent etc.) → jiti + fsCache is faster
#     because jiti aliases resolve to pi's already-loaded modules (shared ESM cache).
#     Bundling these externalizes pi packages but Node loads them fresh = 600ms penalty.
#   - Packages in settings.json → bun bundle to dist/index.mjs for jiti-free load
#
# Run after any source change. pi prefers .js/.mjs over .ts for the same basename.

set -euo pipefail

PI_MONO="$HOME/Projects/personal/pi-mono-fork/packages/coding-agent"
EXT_DIR="$HOME/.pi/agent/extensions"

BUN_EXT="--target=node --format=esm --external=@earendil-works/* --external=@mariozechner/* --external=typebox --external=ulid --external=zod"

echo "▶ Building pi..."
(cd "$PI_MONO" && npm run build)

echo "▶ Compiling simple .ts extensions to .js (native import, no jiti)..."
for ext in notify codex-service-tier handoff; do
  if [[ -f "$EXT_DIR/${ext}.ts" ]]; then
    npx tsc "$EXT_DIR/${ext}.ts" \
      --target ES2022 --module ESNext --moduleResolution Bundler \
      --outDir "$EXT_DIR" --declaration false --skipLibCheck true
    echo "   ${ext}.ts → ${ext}.js"
  fi
done

echo "▶ Building my-pi extensions (skill-loader, tool-search, boot-context-log)..."
bun build "$HOME/Projects/personal/my-pi/extensions/skill-loader/src/index.ts" \
  $BUN_EXT --outfile="$HOME/Projects/personal/my-pi/extensions/skill-loader/dist/index.mjs"
bun build "$HOME/Projects/personal/my-pi/extensions/tool-search/src/index.ts" \
  $BUN_EXT --outfile="$HOME/Projects/personal/my-pi/extensions/tool-search/dist/index.mjs"
bun build "$HOME/Projects/personal/my-pi/extensions/boot-context-log/index.ts" \
  $BUN_EXT --outfile="$HOME/Projects/personal/my-pi/extensions/boot-context-log/dist/index.mjs"

# pi-goal: loaded directly as .ts via jiti — see my-pi/package.json pi.extensions.
# Previous bundling pointed at the pre-migration standalone path (~/Projects/personal/pi-goal/)
# and produced a dist/ that drifted from src. Loading the .ts source kills the drift class.

echo "▶ Building pi-memory..."
bun build "$HOME/Projects/testing/pi-memory/index.ts" \
  $BUN_EXT --outfile="$HOME/Projects/testing/pi-memory/dist/index.mjs"

# pi-semantic-grep: NOT bundled — worker.ts is spawned via import.meta.url at runtime,
# so bundling to dist/ breaks the worker path. jiti + fsCache handles it fine.

echo "▶ Building kilocode-provider..."
bun build "$EXT_DIR/kilocode-provider/index.ts" \
  $BUN_EXT --outfile="$EXT_DIR/kilocode-provider/dist/index.mjs"

echo "▶ Clearing stale jiti cache..."
rm -f "$HOME/.pi/agent/.jiti-cache"/src-*.mjs

echo "✓ Done."
time pi --help > /dev/null

name: pi-cache-stability
description: "Pi prompt-cache hygiene. Use when touching forkAgent, subagents, system prompt, tools, model/tool changes, plan/compaction, cacheWrite, tool search, context modes, or cache-sensitive tool APIs."
---

# Pi Cache Stability

Anthropic's prompt cache is prefix matching: cache hits require the request prefix to be **byte-identical**, use the same model, include the same tools in the same order, and still be **alive within TTL**. Pi forks and extensions break this constantly without realising. Keep them honest.

**Source-of-truth**: `~/Projects/personal/my-pi/docs/cache-strategy.md` — read it before changing anything load-bearing.

**Project memory pointer**: `~/.pi/agent/memory/project/my-pi/project_cache_strategy.md`.

## When This Skill Applies

Load this skill any time you are about to:

- Add or modify a call to `ctx.forkAgent()` in a pi extension.
- Edit `forkAgent`, `_forkAgentFromExtension`, `runChild`, `resolveContextPolicy`, `buildSystemPrompt`, or `overrideBaseSystemPrompt` in `pi-mono-fork/packages/coding-agent`.
- Build a new background agent that runs many times per session (memory extractor, advisor probe, autoresearch worker, condensation fork).
- Investigate "why is this slow / expensive" on a child agent.
- Touch the system prompt order, project context cascade, or skill loader.
- Add or revise model-facing tool APIs, schemas, `promptSnippet`, or `promptGuidelines` (also read `context-engineering/references/model-facing-api-design.md`).
- Change `pi-claude-bridge` cache config.

## Cache Laws

1. **Static first, dynamic last.** Stable system prompt + tool schemas first; project context next; session context/messages last.
2. **Use messages for updates.** Dates, file-change reminders, mode changes, and run status belong in the next user/tool message, not in the cached system prompt.
3. **Do not change models mid-session.** Caches are per-model. Use a subagent handoff instead of switching the parent from Opus/Sonnet to Haiku or vice versa.
4. **Do not add/remove tools mid-session.** Tool definitions are cached prefix. Model state transitions as tools/messages, not schema swaps.
5. **Forks must share the parent prefix.** Compaction, summarization, skill execution, and side computations should reuse the parent's system prompt, tools, and context policy unless the cost is intentional.
6. **Anything that adds content writes to the dynamic boundary, never the static one.** Per-turn or per-session content (advice, status, time, memory recall, reminders, mode banners, run state) must be appended *after* the conversation `cache_control` breakpoint — a trailing `role:"user"`/custom message — never into `systemPrompt`/`systemPrompt:build`/`params.system`/`tools[]` (the static, cached prefix). This is agnostic to the source: it holds for fork-core prompt construction, the harness, the bridge, extensions, and any future injector. The only allowed static-prefix writes are (a) deterministic, value-independent edits (e.g. stripping the volatile `Current date:` line) and (b) one-shot, memoised, byte-stable session-start blocks (e.g. dream-memory's memoised `profile-base`). Test: if the bytes can differ between two turns of the same session, it belongs in the dynamic tail.

**Mid-turn system authority without cache cost.** Need an *authoritative* mid-session instruction (mode switch, operator directive) — not just user-visible reminder text? Append a trailing `role:"user"` message starting with `__PI_MID_SYSTEM__\n`; claude-bridge rewrites it to a real `{role:"system"}` entry after the cache breakpoint (`pi-claude-bridge/index.js` `rewriteMidConversationSystemMessages`; full contract in cache-strategy.md §mid-conversation). Bridge-only — off-bridge the sentinel leaks as literal text. Dormant: no extension uses it yet (2026-06-11).

## Mandatory Checklist Before Merging Fork/Extension Changes

- [ ] **Where does the system prompt come from?** If it's auto-built from parent context, it mutates per session — cache rarely hits. Override with `systemPrompt` or accept the cost knowingly.
- [ ] **Are there per-session substitutions in the system prompt?** (slug, sessionId, paths, timestamps, file lists.) Move them to the user prompt. The system prompt must be byte-stable.
- [ ] **Is prompt order static → dynamic?** System prompt/tools first, project context next, session messages last. No dynamic values before shared stable blocks.
- [ ] **Does this change the model or tool set mid-session?** Use subagent handoffs, mode tools, system-reminder messages, or deferred tool stubs instead.
- [ ] **What is the child's `context` mode?** Default is `"fork"` which inherits the bloated parent prefix. For a focused tool-running child, use `"slim"` or `"none"`.
- [ ] **Is output capped?** A 3-tool child shouldn't burn 1800 output tokens of Opus prose. Pass `maxOutputTokens`.
- [ ] **Is it routed through claude-bridge?** Confirm `BRIDGE_CACHE_TTL` is set (default `1h`).
- [ ] **Did you measure?** Capture a real jsonl after the change. Turn 1 should show `cacheRead / (cacheRead + cacheWrite) ≥ 0.8` once the cache is warm. If turn 1 is still 90% `cacheWrite`, something is mutating between calls.

## References

- Three-layer model, L4 mid-session updates, reference patterns: see `references/cache-internals.md`. Read when implementing or reviewing forkAgent calls or system prompt construction.
- Cache-killer grep patterns, anti-patterns, required bridge headers: see `references/cache-killers.md`. Read when auditing an extension or investigating why cache-write is spiking.
- Routine inspection scripts, quota/caller forensics, Anthropic diagnostics API, verification recipe: see `references/diagnostics.md`. Read when debugging a cache miss or running health checks.

## Related

- `~/Projects/personal/my-pi/docs/cache-strategy.md` — full diagnosis and implementation
- `context-engineering/references/model-facing-api-design.md` — compact model-facing tool API wording and schema review
- `~/.pi/agent/memory/project/my-pi/project_cache_strategy.md` — durable project memory
- `pi-claude-bridge/index.js` — `computePromptFingerprint` / `/cache-divergence` (per-request anchor-split detector). `BRIDGE_FINGERPRINT=off` to disable. **Mirror any change across all runtimes** (MacBook, Mac Mini, lue-kube, Paperclip, Multica).
- `pi-mono-fork/packages/coding-agent/src/core/agents/context.ts` — `resolveContextPolicy`
- `pi-mono-fork/packages/coding-agent/src/core/system-prompt.ts` — prompt order
- `pi-claude-bridge/index.js` — `BRIDGE_CACHE_TTL` config
- Scar: `issue-05-prompt-cache-mutable-counters` (mutable counters bust cache)

## Future Work Pointers

- Skip resource loader entirely when `systemPrompt` is set (small perf win).
- Audit other extensions using `forkAgent` for opt-in to `slim`/`none`.
- Add per-fork `(cacheRead, cacheWrite)` telemetry to `~/.dream-memory/active-recall-events/` for trend visibility.

name: code-craft
description: "Natural/simple code craft: naming, API design, composability, fluent APIs, refactor, simplify, polish, clean code."
---

# Code Craft

Write code that developers want to use. The best APIs feel inevitable, as if they could not have been written any other way.

The standard: code written by someone who cares about the person reading it next.

## Natural Code Standard

This is the required coding style, not a preference.

Code must read naturally and be easy to understand at a glance. It should feel fluent, elegant, obvious, and simple. Names, structure, APIs, functions, variables, methods, classes, syntax, and arguments should make the flow clear enough that a non-programmer could mostly follow what happens.

Prefer clean, efficient, small, modular pieces that compose into larger systems without hiding data flow, logic, or connections. Less is more. Use minimal comments unless asked. Clarity should come from names, structure, and API shape, not explanatory prose.

Avoid over-abstraction, cleverness, noisy indirection, and names or structure that move code away from natural eloquence and simplicity.

## Modes

### Implementation

- Before writing code, name the core concepts and sketch the simplest reader-facing flow.
- During implementation, keep each piece small, direct, and easy to place.
- After implementation, read the diff as a story. Tighten names, flatten flow, remove noise, and replace explanatory comments with clearer code where possible.

### Review

- Review diffs for natural readability, not just correctness.
- Flag vague names, hidden data flow, noisy abstractions, clever control flow, and comments that compensate for unclear code.
- Suggest concrete replacements: better names, smaller functions, simpler APIs, flatter branches, or clearer module boundaries.

## Natural Code Checklist

- [ ] Does this read naturally?
- [ ] Are names obvious?
- [ ] Public verb leak tests: backend swap forces a rename? how-suffix (`WithAdapters`)? two names for one operation (`find`/`search`)? Full tests: `references/principles.md` § 2.
- [ ] Is data flow easy to trace?
- [ ] Is it clear where state lives — who owns it, who mutates it, how long it lasts?
- [ ] Are pieces small and composable?
- [ ] Is there unnecessary abstraction?
- [ ] Could comments be replaced by clearer code?
- [ ] Can a non-specialist roughly follow what happens?

For larger good-code examples, load `references/natural-code-examples.md`.

Brown-field bugfix or surgical patch where over-editing is the risk — minimal-diff discipline: `references/minimal-editing.md`.

## Three Questions

Ask these about every piece of code:

1. **Can I understand this in 5 seconds?** If not, the naming or structure needs work.
2. **Can I extend this without modifying it?** If not, it needs hooks, events, or composition points.
3. **Can I use the simple version simply?** If not, the API is leaking complexity.

---

## Principles

Full rationale + examples for each principle — load when designing APIs, debating names, or reviewing for "why": `references/principles.md`

Principles index: 1. Name Things for the Reader · 2. Name the Layers, Not the Plumbing · 3. Progressive Complexity · 4. Everything Has a Place · 5. Public Verbs Follow the User's Mental Model · 6. Extend Without Modifying · 7. Errors Are for Errors · 8. Types Tell the Story · 9. Compose, Don't Inherit · 10. Design for Chaining · 11. Write Fluent Code · 12. Keep Naming Conventions Deliberate · 13. Use Patterns Intelligently

Classic principles (DI, DRY, SOLID) apply where warranted — inject dependencies at seams for testability, dedupe real duplication (not coincidental similarity) — but natural readability wins when they conflict.

---

## Review Checklist

Full checklist (naming, API surface, extensibility, structure, error handling, DRY) for formal code and API reviews: `references/review-checklist.md`

---

## Audit Workflow

When asked to audit or review a codebase:

1. **Read the entry points** — barrel exports, main classes, public API. Is the surface clean and small?
2. **Map the file structure** — Does each file have a clear purpose? Are there `utils` or `helpers` grab-bags?
3. **Check naming consistency** — Pick a core concept and grep for it. Is the same concept called different things in different places?
4. **Check layer language** — Are entities, relationships, transports, and UI projections named distinctly, or is implementation detail leaking into the top-level API?
5. **Evaluate the extension story** — How would a consumer add new behavior? Do they need to fork, or are there hooks/events/composition points?
6. **Report findings** by severity:
   - **Critical**: Wrong abstraction, leaky interface, naming confusion
   - **Important**: Missing extension points, inconsistent patterns, unnecessary complexity
   - **Suggestions**: Naming improvements, organizational tweaks

For each finding: the problem, the current code, what good looks like, and *why* the change matters.

---

## Writing New Code

1. **Start with the consumer** — Write example usage first. How should this *feel* to call?
2. **Name the vocabulary** — Define core types and interfaces. Get the words right before writing logic.
3. **Separate the layers** — Decide which nouns are entities, relationships, transport details, and UI projections before you write implementation code.
4. **Implement the simple path** — Make the basic use case work with minimal code.
5. **Add extension points** — Only where you have concrete use cases. Not speculatively.
6. **Add the complex path** — Options, hooks, configuration. The simple path stays unchanged.
7. **Document contracts** — Every function that must not throw says so. Every hook documents what it receives and returns.

# Pi development deep reference

Read when changing Pi core/fork internals, extension/profile membership, config layering, native tool definitions, or cache-sensitive prompt/tool behavior.

## Golden rule: no behavior delta in core; route through the platform layer

The fork is ~228 commits ahead of upstream (`earendil-works/pi-mono`) — the goal is **not** to keep it at upstream shape, it is to keep every commit classifiable and the rebase surface shrinkable. Three tiers (grep-verified against upstream):

- **upstream-native** (zero maintenance): `pi.on(event,…)` event bus, `registerTool`, `registerFlag`/`getFlag`, `getActiveTools`/`setActiveTools`, `deepMergeSettings`, `<project_context>` block. Build freely.
- **platform delta** (good, generic, low rebase surface — these are *Luke's own* primitives, **not** upstream): the hooks/filters layer (`addFilter`/`applyFilters`/`removeAction`/`addAction`/`ExtensionHooksAPI`), the cache-split (`splitSystemPromptForCache`, `SYSTEM_PROMPT_DYNAMIC_BOUNDARY`), the `systemPrompt:build` filter, `<system-context>` carrier, agent subsystem, OTEL. They ride on top of the upstream `on()` bus. Write new platform primitives generically so they can be upstream-PR'd (each PR shrinks the rebase surface). Tag in `pi-fork-patch-inventory.md` as `… (platform)`.
- **behavior delta** (forbidden as inline core patches): any opinion about what pi *does* — prompts, tool logic, agent behavior, Luke-specific routing. Route via extension + hook/filter, never inline in `pi-mono-fork` core.

Put customization in an **extension + hook/filter** (wrap+spread a core tool def to override its fields — pattern: `native-tool-overrides` wraps `createEditToolDefinition`). No hook exposes what you need? Add a *new* hook/filter to core (sparingly — each is rebase surface), never an inline behavior patch. Log any unavoidable core change in `my-pi/docs/pi-fork-patch-inventory.md`. Workflow: `my-pi/docs/pi-fork-workflow.md`. Fork-hygiene ADR: `my-pi/docs/adr/0004-fork-hygiene-extract-via-existing-hooks.md`. Active program: `my-pi/docs/goals/goal-2026-05-30T07-50-47Z-pi-platform-program.md`.

## Key repos & paths

| What | Path |
|---|---|
| Pi fork (core binary) | `~/Projects/personal/pi-mono-fork` (coding-agent at `packages/coding-agent`) |
| Personal extension/harness lab | `~/Projects/personal/my-pi` |
| Claude bridge (Anthropic OAuth provider) | `~/Projects/personal/pi-claude-bridge` at `http://127.0.0.1:9100` |
| Extensions | `~/Projects/personal/my-pi/extensions/` (native-tool-overrides, dream-memory, pi-memory, tool-search, skill-loader, time-context, cache-base-prompt, context-forking, advisor, …) |
| Bridge / cache-health / routine launch agents | `~/Library/LaunchAgents/com.pi.claude-bridge.plist`, `com.luke.pi-cache-health.plist`, `com.pi-routine.*.plist` |
| Model metadata (bridge provider) | `~/.pi/agent/models.json` (Opus 4.8 = `claude-opus-4-8`, `forceAdaptiveThinking: true`) |
| Extension API reference / best practices | `pi-mono-fork/packages/coding-agent/docs/extensions.md`, `my-pi/docs/pi-extension-best-practices.md` |
| Setup registry (catalog YAML = source; `generated/` scanner-owned, never hand-edit) | `my-pi/docs/pi-setup/` |
| Runtime fleet map ("where does this pi call go?") | `my-pi/docs/pi-stack-inventory.md` |
| Release engineering (versioned registry, CI gates, rollback, binary dist) | `my-pi/docs/release-engineering.md` |
| Config layering (L1–L4 model, `extensionConfig` contract) | `my-pi/docs/config-layering.md` |

## Native tools (Claude-style aliases)

Registered by `my-pi/extensions/native-tool-overrides/index.ts` (not core — wraps the fork's lowercase factories: capitalized names, arg repair, deferred loading). **Cache-critical: deterministic, one schema per capability — never add/remove/reorder mid-session.**

- Always-loaded: `Read`, `Bash`, `Edit`, `Write`, `Agent`, `Grep`. Deferred (schema on demand): `BashOutput`, `KillShell`, `Find`, `Ls`. Bridge-only markers: `WebFetch`/`WebSearch`.
- Smoke test: `node extensions/native-tool-overrides/test-load.mjs`.

## Tool-input ergonomics

Models call from priors, not your schema → mismatched shapes cause a validation-error loop that burns turns (and on Anthropic can poison the session). Two fixes, **do both**:

1. Make the declared schema the shape the model already reaches for — flat top-level fields over nested wrappers, expected field names, inline example, optional non-essentials.
2. Coerce tolerantly at the boundary, validate strictly inside — one `normalize…()` helper that unwraps legacy wrappers / `JSON.parse`s stringified args / maps aliases.

Keep the *declared* schema cache-stable; coerce in `execute`, not by mutating `tools[]`. Reference impls + full rationale (incl. Claude Code `TaskCreate` parity): `my-pi/extensions/task-tools/src/schema.ts` (`normalizeTaskDraft`), `native-tool-overrides` Edit `prepareArguments`.

## Profiles

A profile = manifest package selecting which extensions (→ hooks/filters/tools/commands) load. Each builds a different system-prompt prefix + tool set → **membership is cache-critical; keep deterministic.**

- `full` (`my-pi/packages/my-pi-full`) local daily driver · `harness` (`…/my-pi-harness`) headless, forbids agent-ui/human-ux · `pod` (`…/my-pi-pod`) minimal k8s/server.
- Per-extension selection, classified (`category` + `profiles`, enforced `forbiddenCategories`) in `my-pi/scripts/check-profiles.mjs`. Load a hook in only some profiles → split it into its own extension, or gate its `pi.hooks.addFilter`/`pi.on` registration on a profile/env flag.
- Add/rename/move an extension → (1) update `packages/my-pi-*/package.json`, (2) classify in `check-profiles.mjs`, (3) `npm --prefix ~/Projects/personal/my-pi run check:profiles`.

## Config layering

Deep detail: `my-pi/docs/config-layering.md`.

| Layer | Name | Mechanism | Example |
|---|---|---|---|
| L1 | Capability | extension source defaults | `const DEFAULT_MAX_TURNS = 5` |
| L2 | Membership | profile manifest `pi.extensions[]` | including/excluding an extension |
| L3 | Tuning | `settings.json` `extensionConfig{}`, deep-merged global ← project | `extensionConfig["cache-base-prompt"].extendBase = true` |
| L4 | Override | env var / CLI `--flag` via `registerFlag`/`getFlag` | `PI_EXTEND_BASE_PROMPT=1` |

- Keep defaults in extension-owned config files or typed source defaults; keep operator tuning in `extensionConfig[yourNamespace]` in `settings.json`; use env vars only as L4 overrides for one-off runs, secrets, CI, or emergency flips.
- New extension settings go in `extensionConfig[yourNamespace]` in `settings.json` — never new top-level `Settings` keys, never env-only configuration.
- `getExtensionConfig(namespace)` accessor on `ExtensionAPI` is the missing ~15 LOC piece (`createExtensionAPI` has no settings handle yet — `loader.ts:254`); track as `fork-first (platform)` until upstreamed. Until it lands, extensions may read `settings.json` directly, then apply env overrides.

## Cache & system-prompt stability

**#1 footgun: changing `params.system` (skill index, Available-tools prose) or the `tools[]` array mid-session bursts the WHOLE conversation cache** — only the stable-system anchor survives. Keep skill index + `tools[]` byte-stable: `defer_loading` stubs in fixed order; never add/remove/reorder mid-session. Deliver genuine mid-task instruction/permission/budget updates as a trailing `role:"user"` text block *after* the conversation `cache_control` breakpoint.

- Any change to `forkAgent`, child agents, system-prompt construction, or background extractors passes the cache-stability review first.
- **Cross-cwd base-extend lever: `PI_EXTEND_BASE_PROMPT=1`** (set in `~/.zshenv` — zsh never sources `~/.profile`, so a copy there is dead). `cache-base-prompt` ext relocates the dynamic boundary so the global AGENTS chain + `<available_skills>` ride **block0** (cross-cwd shared base, cached once) instead of per-cwd **block1** (re-cached per project) — moves ~14K tok cross-cwd, `tools[]` unchanged, content-preserving. Gate: `node extensions/cache-base-prompt/test.mjs`. This is the lever for project/directory-specific caching.
- **`setActiveTools` is NOT idempotent** (fork `agent-harness.ts:941` always emits `tools_update` + a session write, even for an unchanged set — the documented "builtins removed ~2,560×/18d" burst source). An extension calling it per-turn from `before_agent_start` must guard: `if (sameNames(pi.getActiveTools(), desired)) return;` before the call, or it bursts the within-session `tools[]` cache. Pattern: `tool-search`; `advisor` now guarded too.
- Levers/audit/verify: skill `~/.pi/agent/skills/pi-cache-stability/SKILL.md`; source-of-truth `my-pi/docs/cache-strategy.md`; mid-session-burst measurements `my-pi/docs/ws12-system-in-messages-cache.md`. Diagnostics: `pi-cache-stats --all`, `pi-prompt-health --refresh` then `pi-prompt-health`.

- Deferred-tool contracts (situational/heavy extension tools must set `deferLoading: true`): `npm --prefix ~/Projects/personal/my-pi run check:deferred-tool-contracts`. Prefer `tool_reference` / provider-native `defer_loading` over mutating active tools after `tool_search`.
- Verified 2026-06-10: `defer_loading` works through claude-bridge (OAuth `claude-code-20250219` bundle enables it server-side — no explicit `advanced-tool-use` header needed); saves ~17.6k tok/session on my-pi-full. # How I Work

Bias: caution over speed; for trivial tasks use judgment.

## Think Before Coding
- State assumptions explicitly; uncertain → ask. Multiple interpretations → present them, don't pick silently.
- Simpler approach exists → say so; push back when warranted. Confused → stop, name it, ask.

## Simplicity First
- Minimum code that solves the problem; nothing speculative: no features beyond the ask, no abstractions for single-use code, no unrequested configurability, no error handling for impossible scenarios.
- 200 lines that could be 50 → rewrite. Test: would a senior engineer call this overcomplicated?

## Surgical Changes
- Reuse existing types/utilities/patterns before writing new ones; don't broaden public APIs unless required.
- Don't improve adjacent code/comments/formatting; match existing style. Unrelated dead code → mention, don't delete.
- Quality blocking the task → improve it as part of the change, call it out. Real issue outside the task → flag, don't expand scope.
- Remove orphans YOUR change created; leave pre-existing ones. Every changed line traces to the request.

## Goal-Driven Execution
- Verifiable goals: "fix the bug" → "test that reproduces it, make it pass". Multi-step → brief plan, one verify per step.
- Spec work: slices traceable to spec/issue; "what's left?" = concrete file/task deltas; checkpoint before risky refactors.
- Don't fight errors: same error twice → stop, gather evidence (local docs/source first, then web) before the next fix.

Use the current GitHub project by default when the user says "triage" from inside a repo. Use RepoBar as the first pass only for broad queue discovery across profiles/orgs. Prefer a real `repobar` binary when installed. In this workspace it may only exist as a SwiftPM product in `~/Projects/RepoBar`.

```bash
repobar_cmd() {
  if command -v repobar >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    repobar "$@"
  elif [ -x "$HOME/Projects/RepoBar/.build/debug/repobarcli" ]; then
    "$HOME/Projects/RepoBar/.build/debug/repobarcli" "$@"

}

## Local Repo Gate

Before starting work inside any local project, verify the checkout is ready:

```bash
git status --short --branch
git branch --show-current
git pull --ff-only
git status --short --branch

Proceed only when the branch is `main`, the pull succeeds, and the worktree is clean. If the branch is not `main`, the pull fails, or `git status --short` shows changes, stop and ask Peter what to do. Do not switch branches, stash, commit, reset, restore, or clean without explicit direction.

repo=$(gh repo view --json nameWithOwner --jq .nameWithOwner 2>/dev/null || true)
if [ -z "$repo" ]; then

---

# Updating Pi

Pi runs from a local fork build, **not** a published package. Updating Pi means some subset of:

- **A. Sync from upstream** — pull `earendil-works/pi-mono` into the fork's `main`, push to `origin`. *Approval-sensitive (mutates remote).*
- **B. Rebuild the binary** — build the workspace so the local `pi` CLI reflects current code. *Safe, local, reversible.*
- **C. Refresh extensions** — pull Pi-package extensions + reinstall tokenjuice. *Safe, local.*

**These are independent.** Pick the steps the task needs:

- **Full update** ("update pi" / "pull upstream") → do **A → B → C** in order: sync from upstream, rebuild, refresh extensions.
- **My code change isn't live** → just **B** (+ **C** if extensions changed). Do **not** sync upstream merely to rebuild — that's a separate, remote-mutating, approval-sensitive decision.

This replaces the old `rusty-terminal-runtime/scripts/update-pi` script, which conflated all three and always pushed. (`pi update` from a source checkout routes through the `update-pi-agent` wrapper — see the bottom section.)

## Locations

- **Fork**: `~/Projects/personal/pi-mono-fork` (override: `RUSTY_PI_FORK_DIR`). Remotes: `origin` = `valkyriweb/pi-mono`, `upstream` = `earendil-works/pi-mono` (**push DISABLED — never push upstream**).
- **Extension lab**: `~/Projects/personal/my-pi`.
- **Installed CLI**: built `cli.js` at `pi-mono-fork/packages/coding-agent/dist/cli.js`; the `pi` on PATH resolves here.
- **Fork patch inventory**: `~/Projects/personal/my-pi/docs/pi-fork-patch-inventory.md` — every divergence from upstream. Read before resolving non-trivial upstream conflicts.
- **Tokenjuice extension**: generated, self-contained at `~/.pi/agent/extensions/tokenjuice.js` (version-stamped).

---

## A. Sync from upstream  *(approval-sensitive — confirm before pushing)*

### Preflight
- Working tree clean (`git diff --quiet && git diff --cached --quiet`). Stop if dirty.
- On a branch, not detached HEAD. Note the starting branch.

### Fetch + inspect
```bash
cd ~/Projects/personal/pi-mono-fork
git fetch upstream --tags --prune
git log --oneline main..upstream/main   # what's incoming; empty = already current
```

### Sync `main`
```bash
git checkout main
```
- If `main` is an ancestor of `upstream/main` → `git merge --ff-only upstream/main`.
- If `main` already contains `upstream/main` → nothing to do.
- Else (fork commits diverge) → `git merge --no-edit upstream/main`.
- Then **confirm with Luke**, and `git push origin main`.

### Changelog conflicts
Largely solved structurally — should not hard-conflict:
- `*CHANGELOG.md merge=union` (`.gitattributes`) auto-unions both sides on merge/rebase.
- **FORK-CHANGELOG.md owns all fork notes.** Package `CHANGELOG.md` files are upstream-owned; never hand-write fork entries there.
- `.changeset/config.json` has `"changelog": false` (no changeset-github generator fighting upstream's manual Keep-a-Changelog format).
- `scripts/check-changelog-updated.mjs` accepts a `FORK-CHANGELOG.md` touch in place of per-package entries.

If a CHANGELOG still conflicts: take upstream's `[Unreleased]`/version blocks verbatim, keep fork notes only in FORK-CHANGELOG.md, drop any stale fork-authored package-CHANGELOG block.

### Rebase patch branch  *(approval-sensitive — force-push)*
Only if the starting branch ≠ `main`:
```bash
git checkout <branch>
git rebase main
# resolve conflicts (consult the patch inventory), then:
git push origin <branch> --force-with-lease
```
Patch-id-equivalent commits already upstreamed will auto-drop during rebase — expected.

---

## B. Rebuild the binary  *(safe — this is usually all you need)*

**The live `pi` runs a compiled binary, not the JS dist.** The shim `~/.local/bin/pi` execs `packages/coding-agent/dist/pi` — a ~73 MB `bun build --compile` output. A plain `npm run build` only emits the TypeScript→JS (`dist/cli.js`, `dist/bun/cli.js`); it does **not** rebuild `dist/pi`, so code changes won't go live. Use **`build:binary`**:

```bash
cd ~/Projects/personal/pi-mono-fork
# install only if the lockfile moved
git diff --quiet HEAD -- package-lock.json || npm install   # or compare shasum pre/post a pull
# builds tui → ai → agent → coding-agent (JS), THEN bun-compiles dist/pi
( cd packages/coding-agent && npm run build:binary )
```

`build:binary` runs the four package builds in dependency order (`coding-agent` consumes `agent`'s `dist/`, which consumes `ai`, which consumes `tui`) and then `bun build --compile ./dist/bun/cli.js … --outfile dist/pi` + copies binary assets. **Requires `bun` on PATH.** Only those four packages matter for `pi` — **do not** build `mom`, `web-ui`, or `pods`.

Confirm it actually rebuilt: `stat -f '%Sm' packages/coding-agent/dist/pi` should show the current time (a stale mtime means you only built the JS). For a long build, run it backgrounded and capture to a log. **New** `pi` sessions pick up the rebuilt binary; already-running sessions keep their loaded binary until relaunch.

---

## C. Refresh extensions  *(safe — local)*

```bash
# Pi-package extensions (does NOT re-run the source-checkout self-updater):
~/Projects/personal/pi-mono-fork/packages/coding-agent/dist/cli.js update --extensions
```

**Tokenjuice** ships its Pi integration as a generated file at `~/.pi/agent/extensions/tokenjuice.js`, which `pi update --extensions` does **not** touch. Reinstall when the CLI version ≠ the version stamped in that file:
```bash
tokenjuice --version                                   # CLI version
grep -m1 'generated by tokenjuice' ~/.pi/agent/extensions/tokenjuice.js   # stamped version
tokenjuice install pi                                  # if they differ, or file missing
```
Skip silently if `tokenjuice` isn't on PATH.

---

### Codex adapter prompt patch  *(re-verify after every extension refresh)*

`pi update --extensions` can overwrite Luke's local prompt patch in the Codex conversion adapter. After refreshing, confirm the patch survived in `CODEX_GUIDELINES`:
```bash
PATCH="$HOME/.local/share/fnm/node-versions/v24.14.0/installation/lib/node_modules/@howaboua/pi-codex-conversion/src/prompt/build-system-prompt.ts"
grep -nE 'timeout_seconds|tokenjuice wrap|raw logs|write_stdin' "$PATCH"
```
The patch teaches the Codex adapter to: set `timeout_seconds`/`timeout_ms` on hang-prone commands; use `tokenjuice wrap`/`reduce` for noisy output; reduce at source with `jq`/`rg`/`head`/`tail`/`sed -n`; not dump raw logs/JSONL/k8s/traces unless asked; stop polling `write_stdin` after two empty reads. Re-apply if missing. (The `v24.14.0` path drifts with the active fnm Node version — adjust if needed.)

## How `pi update` triggers this  *(source-checkout self-update)*

Built-in `pi update` refreshes extensions but **cannot** self-update a source-checkout install — it errors:
> error: pi cannot self-update this installation. Update @earendil-works/pi-coding-agent using the package manager, wrapper, or source checkout that provides this installation.

So source-checkout updates are routed through a bounded Pi maintenance session via global settings:
```json
"sourceUpdateCommand": ["/Users/luke/Projects/personal/rusty-terminal-runtime/scripts/update-pi-agent"]
```
`scripts/update-pi-agent` launches a non-interactive `pi --print --tools bash,read,grep,find,ls,edit,write` session that prepares an **update branch/worktree**, merges `upstream/main` there, health-checks (`npm run check`), and reports the PR command — deliberately **not** mutating the daily `main` checkout. Wrapper env defaults: `RUSTY_PI_UPDATE_BRANCH` (`lue/pi-upstream-<ts>`), `RUSTY_PI_UPDATE_WORKTREE` (`~/Projects/personal/pi-mono-fork-update`), `RUSTY_PI_UPDATE_HEALTH_CHECK` (`npm run check`), `RUSTY_PI_UPDATE_AGENT_BIN` (pi binary override). When you (an agent) run the update by hand instead, follow sections A–C above directly.

## Verify (gates)

Run the gates for whatever surface you touched:

- **Fork / core**: `npm --prefix ~/Projects/personal/pi-mono-fork run test:build-gate`
- **Extension / profile / cache**: `npm --prefix ~/Projects/personal/my-pi run test:extension-gate`
- **Native tool aliases**: `node ~/Projects/personal/my-pi/extensions/native-tool-overrides/test-load.mjs`
- **Prompt-cache health** (after a real rebuild): `pi-prompt-health --refresh` → send one Pi message → `pi-prompt-health` (compare hit rate / prefix stability).

If you patched fork core (not just extensions), log it in `~/Projects/personal/my-pi/docs/pi-fork-patch-inventory.md` and run both the fork and extension gates.

## Gotchas

- **Don't sync to rebuild.** Upstream is often ahead; pulling it in is a separate, approval-sensitive decision. Rebuild (B) alone fixes "my change isn't live."
- **Never push `upstream`** — its push URL is `DISABLED` on purpose.
- `push origin main` and `--force-with-lease` on a patch branch mutate the remote → confirm with Luke first.
- Build order is load-bearing (tui → ai → agent → coding-agent).
- Fork-changelog entries go in `FORK-CHANGELOG.md`, never in package `CHANGELOG.md`.

## See also

- `~/Projects/agent-scripts/pi-dev.md` — router for hot paths + gates.
- `~/Projects/personal/my-pi/docs/release-engineering.md` — release/versioning/rollback.
- `~/Projects/personal/my-pi/docs/pi-fork-patch-inventory.md` — divergence ledger.
- skill `pi-cache-stability` — before touching cache-sensitive surface.

# Release Engineering

read_when: setting up versioned builds; landing a change to any fork package or extension; debugging non-reproducible pod/clawsweeper images; wiring cache/prompt-stability gates into CI; rolling back a runtime to a known-good version.

---

## Problem: file: links are not a release boundary

Every runtime currently resolves fork packages via `file:` links in `my-pi` root `devDependencies`:

```
"@earendil-works/pi-coding-agent": "file:../pi-mono-fork/packages/coding-agent"
"@earendil-works/pi-agent-core":   "file:../pi-mono-fork/packages/agent"
"@earendil-works/pi-ai":           "file:../pi-mono-fork/packages/ai"
"@earendil-works/pi-tui":          "file:../pi-mono-fork/packages/tui"
```

Consequence: `npm install` on a pod or action runner resolves to whatever the filesystem has at build time. Two builds from the same commit can produce different binaries if the fork checkout differs. Rollback is "re-checkout the fork at some commit and rebuild" — fragile, undocumented, invisible.

The fix is a **versioned registry seam**: publish fork packages and extension/profile packages to a scoped registry; each runtime pins a profile version; rollback = redeploy the previous tag.

---

## Update flow

There are two update lanes; keep them separate:

- **Upstream Pi release available** (startup banner says `New version X is available. Run pi update`): for Luke's source/fork install, run `pi update` only if `settings.sourceUpdateCommand` points at `~/Projects/personal/rusty-terminal-runtime/scripts/update-pi-agent`; otherwise run `~/Projects/personal/rusty-terminal-runtime/scripts/update-pi`. This creates/uses an update branch, merges/rebases upstream into `pi-mono-fork`, runs the fork gate, then refreshes extensions with `pi update --extensions`.
- **Extension/package update available**: run `pi update --extensions` (or `pi update npm:<package>` for one package). This updates installed Pi packages/extensions only; it does not replace the fork checkout or binary.

Fork versions use `0.78.0-luke.N`. The startup version checker should not nag when upstream latest is the same base `0.78.0`; it should nag again when upstream publishes a higher base such as `0.78.1`.

## Registry

**Primary**: GitHub Packages, scope `@valkyriweb`.
- Auth: `NODE_AUTH_TOKEN` = GitHub PAT with `packages:write`. Already available in the `valkyriweb` org.
- Registry URL: `https://npm.pkg.github.com`
- `.npmrc` in fork root and `my-pi` root: `@valkyriweb:registry=https://npm.pkg.github.com`

**Alternate for offline pods**: Verdaccio on `lue-kube` (self-hosted in-cluster registry/proxy that caches `@valkyriweb/*` + public deps). **Decision (2026-05-30): GitHub Packages is primary/source-of-truth; Verdaccio is deferred** — do NOT stand it up until a concrete trigger: (a) a pod/runtime that genuinely cannot reach github.com, (b) GH Packages egress/auth/rate-limit pain once the fleet pulls heavily, or (c) builds must survive a GitHub outage. Until then GH Packages alone is simpler and sufficient. When stood up, track in `docs/pi-stack-inventory.md`.

During development (laptop only): `file:` links remain in place. Kill file: links only for release builds — see "Kill file: links" below.

---

## Three release layers

### Layer 1 — Fork packages (upstream baseline + platform delta)

Packages currently needed by the fork: `@valkyriweb/pi-coding-agent`, `@valkyriweb/pi-agent-core`, `@valkyriweb/pi-ai`, `@valkyriweb/pi-tui`.

**Maintenance policy: upstream by default.** Do **not** publish/control an upstream-maintained support package unless it carries real fork delta required by the coding-agent runtime. If a package has zero fork delta — or its delta is upstreamed/retired — switch that dependency back to the upstream `@earendil-works/*` package and remove the `@valkyriweb` copy from the release set. The only product lifecycle we own is the forked coding-agent runtime; support packages are private, lockstep implementation detail while they differ from upstream.

These are the `@earendil-works/*` fork packages republished under the `@valkyriweb` scope only while needed. Their SemVer version encodes the upstream baseline + the platform-delta commits on top.

Version scheme: `<upstream-version>-luke.<N>` e.g. `0.78.0-luke.3`. Patch bump on each fork-delta release. Major/minor track upstream. Keep support packages lockstep with the CLI; do not give them independent product roadmaps.

Add `publishConfig` to each fork `package.json`:
```json
"publishConfig": { "registry": "https://npm.pkg.github.com", "access": "restricted" }
```

### Layer 2 — Extensions + profile manifests

Each extension under `my-pi/extensions/` and each profile manifest under `my-pi/packages/` becomes its own versioned package with a `peerDependency` on the Layer 1 fork range:

```json
"peerDependencies": {
  "@valkyriweb/pi-coding-agent": ">=0.78.0-luke.0 <0.79.0"
}
```

Published as e.g. `@valkyriweb/pi-native-tool-overrides`, `@valkyriweb/my-pi-full`.

A profile manifest `package.json` declares `dependencies` on the exact extension versions it bundles — this is the "what runs here" bill of materials. Pi package loading does **not** automatically compose sibling packages after npm install: dependent pi packages must be in `dependencies` + `bundledDependencies`, and profile `pi.extensions` paths must reference bundled `node_modules/...` resources (per `pi-mono-fork/packages/coding-agent/docs/packages.md`). Generate release-shaped profile manifests with `npm run profiles:release-manifests`; output goes to ignored `.release/profile-manifests/` for inspection/packaging.

### Layer 3 — Per-runtime lockfile pin

Each runtime (laptop, openclaw, pod, clawsweeper) pins a single profile version in its `package.json` or deployment manifest:

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Launch a Pi maintenance session to prepare a safe source-checkout update.
# This is intended for settings.sourceUpdateCommand so `pi update` creates an
# update branch and health-checks it instead of mutating the daily main checkout.

set -euo pipefail

REPO_ROOT="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/.." && pwd)"
FORK_DIR="${RUSTY_PI_FORK_DIR:-$HOME/Projects/personal/pi-mono-fork}"
PI_BIN="${RUSTY_PI_UPDATE_AGENT_BIN:-pi}"
UPDATE_BRANCH="${RUSTY_PI_UPDATE_BRANCH:-lue/pi-upstream-$(date +%Y%m%d-%H%M%S)}"
UPDATE_WORKTREE="${RUSTY_PI_UPDATE_WORKTREE:-$HOME/Projects/personal/pi-mono-fork-update}"
HEALTH_CHECK="${RUSTY_PI_UPDATE_HEALTH_CHECK:-npm run check}"

PROMPT=$(printf '%s\n' \
  "You are a Pi maintenance agent running because Luke typed \`pi update\`." \
  "" \
  "Goal: prepare a safe update branch for Luke's source-checkout Pi installation." \
  "" \
  "Work from this repo unless inspection requires another cwd:" \
  "" \
  "  $FORK_DIR" \
  "" \
  "Update branch:" \
  "" \
  "  $UPDATE_BRANCH" \
  "" \
  "Update worktree:" \
  "" \
  "  $UPDATE_WORKTREE" \
  "" \
  "Health check:" \
  "" \
  "  $HEALTH_CHECK" \
  "" \
  "Rules:" \
  "- Do not ask Luke questions unless the update is blocked by a conflict or destructive choice." \
  "- First inspect git status, branch state, remotes, and worktrees in $FORK_DIR." \
  "- Do not stash, merge into, push to, or otherwise mutate daily main." \
  "- If $FORK_DIR is dirty or not on main, stop and report the exact files/branch." \
  "- Fetch origin and upstream with tags/prune." \
  "- Ensure local main is a clean fast-forward of origin/main only; do not merge upstream into main." \
  "- Create or reuse $UPDATE_BRANCH in $UPDATE_WORKTREE from origin/main." \
  "- Merge upstream/main into $UPDATE_BRANCH inside $UPDATE_WORKTREE." \
  "- Resolve only mechanical merge conflicts. Stop for product choices or cache/tool semantics you cannot prove safe." \
  "- Run the health check in $UPDATE_WORKTREE: $HEALTH_CHECK." \
  "- On success, report branch, worktree, HEAD, health-check result, and the exact PR command for Luke to run if review passes.")

cd "$REPO_ROOT"
"$PI_BIN" \
  --print \
  --tools bash,read,grep,find,ls,edit,write \
  "$PROMPT"
AGENT_EXIT=$?

# Verify the fork/update worktree are in a clean post-update state. The agent
# can exit 0 after reporting an unresolved conflict; without this check, pi's
# caller would then print "Updated pi" despite an in-progress merge/rebase.
verify_no_in_progress_git_operation() {
  local repo_dir="$1"

  if [[ ! -d "$repo_dir" ]]; then
    return 0
  fi

  local git_dir_path
  git_dir_path="$(git -C "$repo_dir" rev-parse --git-dir 2>/dev/null || echo "$repo_dir/.git")"
  if [[ -e "$git_dir_path/MERGE_HEAD" ]]; then
    echo "error: merge in progress in $repo_dir; resolve before rerunning pi update" >&2
    exit 1
  fi
  if [[ -d "$git_dir_path/rebase-merge" || -d "$git_dir_path/rebase-apply" ]]; then
    echo "error: rebase in progress in $repo_dir; resolve before rerunning pi update" >&2
    exit 1
  fi
  if git -C "$repo_dir" ls-files --unmerged | grep -q .; then
    echo "error: unmerged paths remain in $repo_dir" >&2
    exit 1
  fi
}

verify_no_in_progress_git_operation "$FORK_DIR"
verify_no_in_progress_git_operation "$UPDATE_WORKTREE"

exit "$AGENT_EXIT"

- `fork-first` — mature/upstreamable, but Luke's decision is to validate in the fork first and PR upstream later.
- `extension-portable` — move to `my-pi` package once the required hook exists.
- `hook-surface` — desired steady-state fork patch: additive vendor-neutral hooks only.
- `drop` — remove from the fork.
- `retired` — already removed or no longer needed.
- `upstreamed` — equivalent upstream behavior exists; remove local patch after sync.

### Delta tier (append in parentheses to the State cell, inline — no separate column)

Classify each patch by which tier of change it is — this determines upstream-PR candidacy and rebase cost:

- `(upstream)` — uses only upstream-native primitives; zero delta. Should not need an inventory row.
- `(platform)` — generic, vendor-neutral primitive layered on the upstream `on()` bus (hooks/filters, cache-split, OTEL seams, `getExtensionConfig`). Good. Write generically; upstream when mature.
- `(behavior)` — encodes an opinion about what pi does (prompt text, tool logic, agent behavior, Luke-specific routing). Acceptable only in extensions; flag for extraction if found inline in core.

Example: `fork-first (platform)` = mature generic primitive, validate in fork before upstreaming. `active (behavior)` found here = move to an extension. Back-fill the tier on each row as it's next touched; no bulk rewrite needed.

## Hook batches

Steady-state goal: the fork carries only small, additive hook-surface patches in core; behavior moves to `my-pi` packages.

1. **B1 — renderers + lifecycle:** `setDefaultMessageRenderer`, `onSessionDispose`, `ctx.registerLiveSession`/`getLiveSession`, `ctx.subscribeTaskMessages`.
2. **B2 — agent registry:** `pi.agents[]`, `registerAgentDefinitions`, `pi.chains[]`, `ctx.registerContextMode`, `BeforeChildAgentStartEvent` with session ref.
3. **B3 — run registry:** `ctx.registerRunRegistry` / `ctx.getRunRegistry`.
4. **B4 — session factory + instrument points:** `ctx.createChildSession`, provider/compaction/tool-call before/after hooks, `ctx.registerTelemetry`.
5. **B5 — TUI panes:** `registerOverlay`, `registerFooterFocusable`, `registerMainPane`.

## Workflow decisions

- Fork-first only: all standalone fixes and hooks stay in the fork until Luke validates the local end-to-end architecture.
- No speculative OSS PRs. Upstream PRs happen later, one small themed patch at a time, with tests/docs/justification.
- Spicy hook fallback: if upstream rejects `ctx.createChildSession` or `registerMainPane`, keep that hook as an additive fork patch and keep the consumer package working against Luke's fork.

## Rebase checklist

Before rebasing or updating the fork:

1. Fetch upstream and origin.
2. Compare patch stack:
   ```bash
   git log --oneline upstream/main..HEAD
   git diff --stat upstream/main...HEAD
   ```
3. Check this inventory against `my-pi/docs/plans/fork-hygiene-audit.md`.
4. For each patch, mark `upstreamed`, `retired`, `fork-first`, `extension-portable`, or still `active`.
5. Rebase/cherry-pick one logical patch at a time.
6. Run focused verification for each carried patch.
7. Update this inventory and `FORK-CHANGELOG.md` when a patch is added, retired, upstreamed, or moved to my-pi.

# How I Work

Bias: caution over speed; for trivial tasks use judgment.

## Think Before Coding
- State assumptions explicitly; uncertain → ask. Multiple interpretations → present them, don't pick silently.
- Simpler approach exists → say so; push back when warranted. Confused → stop, name it, ask.

## Simplicity First
- Minimum code that solves the problem; nothing speculative: no features beyond the ask, no abstractions for single-use code, no unrequested configurability, no error handling for impossible scenarios.
- 200 lines that could be 50 → rewrite. Test: would a senior engineer call this overcomplicated?

## Surgical Changes
- Reuse existing types/utilities/patterns before writing new ones; don't broaden public APIs unless required.
- Don't improve adjacent code/comments/formatting; match existing style. Unrelated dead code → mention, don't delete.
- Quality blocking the task → improve it as part of the change, call it out. Real issue outside the task → flag, don't expand scope.
- Remove orphans YOUR change created; leave pre-existing ones. Every changed line traces to the request.

## Goal-Driven Execution
- Verifiable goals: "fix the bug" → "test that reproduces it, make it pass". Multi-step → brief plan, one verify per step.
- Spec work: slices traceable to spec/issue; "what's left?" = concrete file/task deltas; checkpoint before risky refactors.
- Don't fight errors: same error twice → stop, gather evidence (local docs/source first, then web) before the next fix.

## Code Quality

## Execution Policy
- Clear + reversible → act. Irreversible/destructive/private/external (send/post/delete/deploy) → ask first.
- One non-retrievable decision blocking safe progress → one concise question, not three.
- Newest user instruction wins conflicts.

## Tool Discipline
- Tool evidence over recall for action, state, or mutable facts; concrete path from user → `Read` it before asking.
- Smallest native parser: `jq` for JSON; `Read` for files; `Grep` for known text.
- Expensive/remote commands: run once, save to `/tmp`, inspect the file.
- Verify before deciding: classify from a concrete artifact (log line, test output, file:line). Test: *what evidence would change my mind?*
- 3-strike rule: same tool + same input 3× → stop; write what's known, what's unknown, and a different action.

## Agent & Tool Routing
- Read-only multi-file investigation → exploration agent. Implementation/mixed → general-purpose. Diff review → reviewer. Design-before-code → plan. Known file/symbol/error, ≤3 files → direct tools, no agent.
- Model floors: scouting → fast/low; mechanical edits → medium; planning/API design/migrations and adversarial review/architecture/security → frontier/high. Never fast/mini models for review, security, architecture, or completion audits for large tasks.
- GitHub URLs → prefer `gh`. WebSearch for past-cutoff/current/version-specific info; include the year. Cheap-and-narrow beats expensive-and-fuzzy.

## Skill Auto-load
Load the matching skill **before** the first tool call in that domain — auto-trigger isn't reliable. Don't claim a skill was used unless actually loaded. Skill wrappers beat raw runbook commands.

## Instruction & Skill Maintenance
- Budgets: skill `description` ≤250 chars = capability + "use when" triggers; SKILL.md body ≤~120 lines — rules/workflow inline, lookup tables & runbooks → `references/` with read-when pointers. Parents stay thin routers; demote children via `skillOverrides` in `~/.claude/settings.json`.
- New always-loaded line: falsifiable + traces to a real failure; prefer a hook/test over more prose. Compressing: snapshot to `backups/<date>-<slug>/` first, loss-audit (distinctive-token Grep old vs new) after.
- Deploy skills: `python3 scripts/skills link --apply` (symlinks → Claude/Codex/Pi); dry-run first.

## Hygiene & Completion
- Stale docs/skills/contradictions spotted while working: fix small things in place; surface non-trivial/cross-cutting for approval; ask when intent unclear. Don't ignore rot.
- Todo incomplete until every requested item handled or marked **[blocked]**: *"items 1–3 done; 4 [blocked]: need <X>"*. Before "done": claims grounded + smallest meaningful gate run (test/typecheck/lint/build/screenshot/diff) — or say why none could.

## Z/L Continuum — Code Review Tiers
Classify every change at top of reply; ambiguous → classify up; user override wins.

| Tier | Scope | Handoff |
|---|---|---|
| **critical** | Core behavior of what's shipping now | Stop per diff, wait for approval; one critical → one cycle |
| **important** | Adjacent features, cross-cutting refactors, non-obvious intent | Batch diffs, summarize, wait for "go" |
| **routine** | Tests, fixtures, docs, lint/format, codegen, styling | Proceed; report at end |

## Communication
- Correctness over voice; style never trumps answer/format/safety. Lead with outcome; cite artifacts (paths, commands, errors). One-sentence narration before meaningful tool use, then the call in the same turn.
- Blocked on Luke for attention-sensitive input (auth, 1Password, npm/release gates, approvals, blockers) → `sag-luke --volume 0.65 "<short specific ask>"` + same request in chat. Rare and specific; never routine status.
- Wrong assumption would waste work (ambiguous scope, planning fork, `grill-with-docs` interrogation, either/or) → `AskUserQuestion` with 2–4 concrete options; one round, then proceed. Trivial/reversible → just act. Denied tool call you don't understand, or not clear → ask via `AskUserQuestion`.

## Parallel & Long Sessions
- Independent tasks → parallel; dependent → sequential. High-volume output → agent or background; multi-agent comms via temp files.
- Long sessions: exploration agents first for >5-file refactors; after architecture-heavy slices report done/yet-to-do, deviations, roadblocks; cross-session threads → `/tmp` handoff.

## Learning
- Capture failure patterns (mode, detection signal, prevention rule) per `prompts/learning-scars.md`: `- YYYY-MM-DD: "lesson" (context) → SCARS/<issue>.md`.
- When corrected, encode the falsifiable rule where it'll be re-read — AGENTS.md, the skill, or a test/hook — not just this conversation (the ratchet). Every durable rule traces to a specific failure.

name: pi-update
description: "Update the local Pi (pi-mono fork): sync from upstream, integrate fork patches, rebuild the coding-agent binary, refresh extensions. Use when updating Pi, pulling upstream into the fork, or rebuilding so the local `pi` CLI picks up code changes."
---

# Updating Pi

Pi runs from a local fork build, **not** a published package. Updating Pi means some subset of:

- **A. Sync from upstream** — pull `earendil-works/pi-mono` into the fork's `main`, push to `origin`. *Approval-sensitive (mutates remote).*
- **B. Rebuild the binary** — build the workspace so the local `pi` CLI reflects current code. *Safe, local, reversible.*
- **C. Refresh extensions** — pull Pi-package extensions + reinstall tokenjuice. *Safe, local.*

**These are independent.** Pick the steps the task needs:

- **Full update** ("update pi" / "pull upstream") → do **A → B → C** in order: sync from upstream, rebuild, refresh extensions.
- **My code change isn't live** → just **B** (+ **C** if extensions changed). Do **not** sync upstream merely to rebuild — that's a separate, remote-mutating, approval-sensitive decision.

This replaces the old `rusty-terminal-runtime/scripts/update-pi` script, which conflated all three and always pushed. (`pi update` from a source checkout routes through the `update-pi-agent` wrapper — see the bottom section.)

## Locations

- **Fork**: `~/Projects/personal/pi-mono-fork` (override: `RUSTY_PI_FORK_DIR`). Remotes: `origin` = `valkyriweb/pi-mono`, `upstream` = `earendil-works/pi-mono` (**push DISABLED — never push upstream**).
- **Extension lab**: `~/Projects/personal/my-pi`.
- **Installed CLI**: built `cli.js` at `pi-mono-fork/packages/coding-agent/dist/cli.js`; the `pi` on PATH resolves here.
- **Fork patch inventory**: `~/Projects/personal/my-pi/docs/pi-fork-patch-inventory.md` — every divergence from upstream. Read before resolving non-trivial upstream conflicts.
- **Tokenjuice extension**: generated, self-contained at `~/.pi/agent/extensions/tokenjuice.js` (version-stamped).

---

## A. Sync from upstream  *(approval-sensitive — confirm before pushing)*

### Preflight
- Working tree clean (`git diff --quiet && git diff --cached --quiet`). Stop if dirty.
- On a branch, not detached HEAD. Note the starting branch.

### Fetch + inspect
```bash
cd ~/Projects/personal/pi-mono-fork
git fetch upstream --tags --prune
git log --oneline main..upstream/main   # what's incoming; empty = already current
```

### Sync `main`
```bash
git checkout main
```
- If `main` is an ancestor of `upstream/main` → `git merge --ff-only upstream/main`.
- If `main` already contains `upstream/main` → nothing to do.
- Else (fork commits diverge) → `git merge --no-edit upstream/main`.
- Then **confirm with Luke**, and `git push origin main`.

### Changelog conflicts
Largely solved structurally — should not hard-conflict:
- `*CHANGELOG.md merge=union` (`.gitattributes`) auto-unions both sides on merge/rebase.
- **FORK-CHANGELOG.md owns all fork notes.** Package `CHANGELOG.md` files are upstream-owned; never hand-write fork entries there.
- `.changeset/config.json` has `"changelog": false` (no changeset-github generator fighting upstream's manual Keep-a-Changelog format).
- `scripts/check-changelog-updated.mjs` accepts a `FORK-CHANGELOG.md` touch in place of per-package entries.

If a CHANGELOG still conflicts: take upstream's `[Unreleased]`/version blocks verbatim, keep fork notes only in FORK-CHANGELOG.md, drop any stale fork-authored package-CHANGELOG block.

### Rebase patch branch  *(approval-sensitive — force-push)*
Only if the starting branch ≠ `main`:
```bash
git checkout <branch>
git rebase main
# resolve conflicts (consult the patch inventory), then:
git push origin <branch> --force-with-lease
```
Patch-id-equivalent commits already upstreamed will auto-drop during rebase — expected.

---

## B. Rebuild the binary  *(safe — this is usually all you need)*

**The live `pi` runs a compiled binary, not the JS dist.** The shim `~/.local/bin/pi` execs `packages/coding-agent/dist/pi` — a ~73 MB `bun build --compile` output. A plain `npm run build` only emits the TypeScript→JS (`dist/cli.js`, `dist/bun/cli.js`); it does **not** rebuild `dist/pi`, so code changes won't go live. Use **`build:binary`**:

```bash
cd ~/Projects/personal/pi-mono-fork
# install only if the lockfile moved
git diff --quiet HEAD -- package-lock.json || npm install   # or compare shasum pre/post a pull
# builds tui → ai → agent → coding-agent (JS), THEN bun-compiles dist/pi
( cd packages/coding-agent && npm run build:binary )
```

`build:binary` runs the four package builds in dependency order (`coding-agent` consumes `agent`'s `dist/`, which consumes `ai`, which consumes `tui`) and then `bun build --compile ./dist/bun/cli.js … --outfile dist/pi` + copies binary assets. **Requires `bun` on PATH.** Only those four packages matter for `pi` — **do not** build `mom`, `web-ui`, or `pods`.

Confirm it actually rebuilt: `stat -f '%Sm' packages/coding-agent/dist/pi` should show the current time (a stale mtime means you only built the JS). For a long build, run it backgrounded and capture to a log. **New** `pi` sessions pick up the rebuilt binary; already-running sessions keep their loaded binary until relaunch.

---

## C. Refresh extensions  *(safe — local)*

```bash
# Pi-package extensions (does NOT re-run the source-checkout self-updater):
~/Projects/personal/pi-mono-fork/packages/coding-agent/dist/cli.js update --extensions
```

**Tokenjuice** ships its Pi integration as a generated file at `~/.pi/agent/extensions/tokenjuice.js`, which `pi update --extensions` does **not** touch. Reinstall when the CLI version ≠ the version stamped in that file:
```bash
tokenjuice --version                                   # CLI version
grep -m1 'generated by tokenjuice' ~/.pi/agent/extensions/tokenjuice.js   # stamped version
tokenjuice install pi                                  # if they differ, or file missing
```
Skip silently if `tokenjuice` isn't on PATH.

---

### Codex adapter prompt patch  *(re-verify after every extension refresh)*

`pi update --extensions` can overwrite Luke's local prompt patch in the Codex conversion adapter. After refreshing, confirm the patch survived in `CODEX_GUIDELINES`:
```bash
PATCH="$HOME/.local/share/fnm/node-versions/v24.14.0/installation/lib/node_modules/@howaboua/pi-codex-conversion/src/prompt/build-system-prompt.ts"
grep -nE 'timeout_seconds|tokenjuice wrap|raw logs|write_stdin' "$PATCH"
```
The patch teaches the Codex adapter to: set `timeout_seconds`/`timeout_ms` on hang-prone commands; use `tokenjuice wrap`/`reduce` for noisy output; reduce at source with `jq`/`rg`/`head`/`tail`/`sed -n`; not dump raw logs/JSONL/k8s/traces unless asked; stop polling `write_stdin` after two empty reads. Re-apply if missing. (The `v24.14.0` path drifts with the active fnm Node version — adjust if needed.)

## How `pi update` triggers this  *(source-checkout self-update)*

Built-in `pi update` refreshes extensions but **cannot** self-update a source-checkout install — it errors:
> error: pi cannot self-update this installation. Update @earendil-works/pi-coding-agent using the package manager, wrapper, or source checkout that provides this installation.

So source-checkout updates are routed through a bounded Pi maintenance session via global settings:
```json
"sourceUpdateCommand": ["/Users/luke/Projects/personal/rusty-terminal-runtime/scripts/update-pi-agent"]
```
`scripts/update-pi-agent` launches a non-interactive `pi --print --tools bash,read,grep,find,ls,edit,write` session that prepares an **update branch/worktree**, merges `upstream/main` there, health-checks (`npm run check`), and reports the PR command — deliberately **not** mutating the daily `main` checkout. Wrapper env defaults: `RUSTY_PI_UPDATE_BRANCH` (`lue/pi-upstream-<ts>`), `RUSTY_PI_UPDATE_WORKTREE` (`~/Projects/personal/pi-mono-fork-update`), `RUSTY_PI_UPDATE_HEALTH_CHECK` (`npm run check`), `RUSTY_PI_UPDATE_AGENT_BIN` (pi binary override). When you (an agent) run the update by hand instead, follow sections A–C above directly.

## Verify (gates)

Run the gates for whatever surface you touched:

- **Fork / core**: `npm --prefix ~/Projects/personal/pi-mono-fork run test:build-gate`
- **Extension / profile / cache**: `npm --prefix ~/Projects/personal/my-pi run test:extension-gate`
- **Native tool aliases**: `node ~/Projects/personal/my-pi/extensions/native-tool-overrides/test-load.mjs`
- **Prompt-cache health** (after a real rebuild): `pi-prompt-health --refresh` → send one Pi message → `pi-prompt-health` (compare hit rate / prefix stability).

If you patched fork core (not just extensions), log it in `~/Projects/personal/my-pi/docs/pi-fork-patch-inventory.md` and run both the fork and extension gates.

## Gotchas

- **Don't sync to rebuild.** Upstream is often ahead; pulling it in is a separate, approval-sensitive decision. Rebuild (B) alone fixes "my change isn't live."
- **Never push `upstream`** — its push URL is `DISABLED` on purpose.
- `push origin main` and `--force-with-lease` on a patch branch mutate the remote → confirm with Luke first.
- Build order is load-bearing (tui → ai → agent → coding-agent).
- Fork-changelog entries go in `FORK-CHANGELOG.md`, never in package `CHANGELOG.md`.

- `~/Projects/agent-scripts/pi-dev.md` — router for hot paths + gates.

- `~/Projects/personal/my-pi/docs/pi-fork-patch-inventory.md` — divergence ledger.

# GitHub Publish Changes

## Overview

Use this skill only when the user explicitly wants the full publish flow from the local checkout: branch setup if needed, staging, commit, push, and opening a pull request.

This workflow is hybrid:

- Use local `git` for branch creation, staging, commit, and push.
- Prefer the GitHub app from this plugin for pull request creation after the branch is on the remote.
- Use `gh` as a fallback for current-branch PR discovery, auth checks, or PR creation when the connector path cannot infer the repository or head branch cleanly.

## Prerequisites

- Require GitHub CLI `gh`. Check `gh --version`. If missing, ask the user to install `gh` and stop.
- Require authenticated `gh` session. Run `gh auth status`. If not authenticated, ask the user to run `gh auth login` (and re-run `gh auth status`) before continuing.
- Require a local git repository with a clean understanding of which changes belong in the PR.

## Naming conventions

- Branch: `codex/{description}` when starting from main/master/default.
- Commit: `{description}` (terse).
- PR title: `[codex] {description}` summarizing the full diff.

## Workflow

1. Confirm intended scope.
   - Run `git status -sb` and inspect the diff before staging.
   - If the working tree contains unrelated changes, do not default to `git add -A`. Ask the user which files belong in the PR.
2. Determine the branch strategy.
   - If on `main`, `master`, or another default branch, create `codex/{description}`.
   - Otherwise stay on the current branch.
3. Stage only the intended changes.
   - Prefer explicit file paths when the worktree is mixed.
   - Use `git add -A` only when the user has confirmed the whole worktree belongs in scope.
4. Commit tersely with the confirmed description.
5. Run the most relevant checks available if they have not already been run.
   - If checks fail due to missing dependencies or tools, install what is needed and rerun once.
6. Push with tracking: `git push -u origin $(git branch --show-current)`.
7. Open a draft PR.
   - Prefer the GitHub app from this plugin for PR creation after the push succeeds.
   - Derive `repository_full_name` from the remote, for example by normalizing `git remote get-url origin` or by using `gh repo view --json nameWithOwner`.
   - Derive `head_branch` from `git branch --show-current`.
   - Derive `base_branch` from the user request when specified; otherwise use the remote default branch, for example via `gh repo view --json defaultBranchRef`.
   - If the branch is being pushed from a fork or the PR target differs from the remote that was just pushed, prefer `gh pr create` fallback because the connector PR creation flow expects one repository target and may not encode cross-repo head semantics cleanly.
   - If connector-based PR creation cannot infer the repository or branch cleanly, fall back to `gh pr create --draft --fill --head $(git branch --show-current)`.
   - Write the PR body to a temp file with real newlines when using CLI fallback so the markdown renders cleanly.
8. Summarize the result with branch name, commit, PR target, validation, and anything the user still needs to confirm.

## Write Safety

- Never stage unrelated user changes silently.
- Never push without confirming scope when the worktree is mixed.
- Default to a draft PR unless the user explicitly asks for a ready-for-review PR.
- If the repository does not appear to be connected to an accessible GitHub remote, stop and explain the blocker before making assumptions.

## PR Body Expectations

The PR description should use real Markdown prose and cover:

- what changed
- why it changed
- the user or developer impact
- the root cause when the PR is a fix
- the checks used to validate it

# Fork Changelog

Fork-specific changes maintained by valkyriweb. Upstream package changelogs stay reserved for upstream release notes and upstreamable changes.

## [Unreleased]

### Fixed

- **Background-job wakes survived two failure modes that left idle sessions parked forever** (`packages/coding-agent/src/core/tools/bash.ts`, `core/agent-session.ts`; entry covers `b1fcbc66`). (1) **Crash/signal-death of a `run_in_background` bash job was silently swallowed** — the exit handler only fired the terminal notification for a clean `"exited"` status, so a process killed by a signal (SIGSEGV, OOM SIGKILL, an external SIGTERM) landed as `"killed"` and never woke the agent. It now wakes on any terminal transition the agent did *not* initiate: deliberate stops (`bash_kill`/dispose/`killAll`) flip status off `"running"` *before* the exit fires and stay silent as before, but a signal death while still `"running"` now notifies (status `killed`, with `signal`). This silence is now race-safe on both edges: a deliberate `bash_kill` whose target already exited (`killProcessTree` throws `ESRCH`) still marks the job `killed` (and reports success) instead of leaving it `"running"` and tripping a spurious wake, and both background `error` handlers gained the same `wasRunning` gate so a `spawn`-error event on an already-stopped job stays silent too (regression test `test/bash-bg-kill-esrch.test.ts`). (2) **The idle-wake debounce timer dropped the wake if it fired mid-compaction** — the fire-once timer was already cleared, so a threshold/overflow compaction overlapping the 300 ms window stranded the notification in history with no retry; it now re-arms one debounce window later and fires once genuinely idle. Both paths covered by regression tests proven to fail on baseline and pass with the fix (`test/bash-background.test.ts`, `test/suite/agent-session-wake-on-idle.test.ts`). CC `<task-notification>` parity: a crashed/killed background job is a first-class terminal event, not a special silent path.

### Added

- **Extension event contexts can reload runtime resources directly** (`packages/coding-agent/src/core/extensions/{types,runner}.ts`, `core/agent-session.ts`, `modes/interactive/interactive-mode.ts`). `ctx.reload()` is now available on normal extension event handlers, not only slash-command handlers, so provider-family model-switch extensions can rebuild extension/package membership before the next provider request without queuing a slash command into the transcript. Regression: `packages/coding-agent/test/extensions-runner.test.ts` asserts `ExtensionContext.reload()` calls the bound runtime reload action.

### Fixed

- **Background bash jobs now wake the agent on completion (`#bash-bg-completion-wake`) — the documented notification was never wired for bash.** A `run_in_background:true` bash command ran, completed, updated the TUI footer via `notifyBashBgJobsChanged()`, and pushed **nothing** to the model. Only background *agent* runs had a wake path (`onBackgroundTerminal` → `AgentSession._emitAgentCompletion` → `sendCustomMessage`); the bash tool description still inherited Claude Code's promise ("you'll be notified when it finishes") and `core/tools/background-tasks.ts` even documented "Output is push-notified on completion", but the bash side of that wiring never existed. Net effect: a CC-trained model narrated "they'll wake me when done" and parked forever on a wake that never came. Fix mirrors the agent path: a `subscribeBashBgTerminal` listener registry in `core/tools/bash.ts` fires once on **natural** termination only (process exit / spawn error — explicit `bash_kill`, `killAll`, and session dispose deliberately do **not** fire, since the agent already knows it stopped them); `AgentSession.emitBashCompletion(job)` builds a `<task_notification>` custom message (task id, status, exit code, command, elapsed, output log path) and delivers it via `deliverAs: "followUp"` exactly like `_emitAgentCompletion`; the single **main interactive session** wires the subscription in `interactive-mode.ts` (the bg-bash store is process-global, so subscribing here rather than in every forked child session avoids duplicate notifications). The bash tool description + guideline were reworded to truthfully promise the wake and tell the model not to poll or re-run to "check" (one-time `tools[]` cache re-warm, then stable). Regression: `test/bash-background.test.ts` (natural-exit fires once with `status: exited`/`exit 0`; explicit kill fires zero times). Logged in `my-pi/docs/pi-fork-patch-inventory.md`.
- **Release publish no longer 422s on the upstream changelog size ("body is too long").** The `Release` workflow used `changesets/action`'s default `createGithubReleases: true`, which builds each package's GitHub Release body by matching a heading whose text equals the version (`## 0.31.0`). The fork's package `CHANGELOG.md` files are upstream-owned Keep-a-Changelog (`## [0.31.0] - 2026-01-02`, `coding-agent` is 400KB+ via `merge=union`), so the match always fails and the action falls back to dumping the **entire file** as the body — exceeding GitHub's 125000-char Release-body cap → `422` → the whole publish job reds (sometimes after publishing to the registry but before every Release is cut). Set `createGithubReleases: false` and added `.github/scripts/create-github-releases.mjs`, a post-publish step that cuts a Release per just-published package (from `steps.changesets.outputs.publishedPackages`) with a small, bounded body pointing at `FORK-CHANGELOG.md` — never the upstream changelog. The upstream-owned changelogs and `merge=union` are left untouched (slimming them is deferred to a separate ownership change with its own ADR). Idempotent (skips packages that already have a Release). Mirrors the same fix in the `my-pi` repo (#139).
