Design [`docs/plans/b5-tui-hooks-design-proposal-2026-05-21.md`](my-pi/docs/plans/b5-tui-hooks-design-proposal-2026-05-21.md) approved by Luke 2026-05-22; 14 unit tests in `extensions-runner-b5-hooks.test.ts` cover registration, show/hide delegation, first-registration-wins, reactive footer visibility, and no-registration baseline.
- Added `triggerTokens` to `compaction` settings — an absolute context-token threshold for auto-compaction. When the active model's context window is known, Pi derives `reserveTokens` as `contextWindow - triggerTokens`; otherwise falls back to the configured `reserveTokens`. Not yet upstream (FORK-CHANGELOG previously claimed PR #5 — that PR is unrelated; no upstream PR exists for this change as of 2026-05-21).
- Added `run_in_background`, `bash_output(bgId)`, and `bash_kill(bgId)` to the built-in `bash` tool, mirroring Claude Code's `BashOutput`/`KillShell` API. Background jobs spawn detached (POSIX), append stdout/stderr to `~/.pi/agent/bash-bg/<bgId>.log`, and the registry is reaped via `killAllBashBgJobs()` from `AgentSession.dispose()` so processes don't leak across `/clear`, fork, switchSession, reload, or final shutdown. Bounded log slices for `bash_output`, idempotent `bash_kill`, and a teardown test that confirms registry cleanup.
- Added `settings.subagents` — default model and thinking config for native child agents. Supports a global `defaults` block and a `providers[<parent.provider>]` map. Precedence: explicit task option > agent frontmatter > `subagents.providers[parent.provider]` > `subagents.defaults` > parent inheritance. Wired end-to-end through `runChild` and `resumeSingleBackgroundRun` via a new `resolveAgentDefaults()` helper; covered by one unit test per precedence layer plus an integration test that reads through `SettingsManager.getSubagentSettings()`.
- **Phase 2b** — Real-session rendering in the TUI zoom view. When zooming into a running background agent, the view now subscribes to the child `AgentSession`'s live event stream and renders its transcript using `AssistantMessageComponent` and `ToolExecutionComponent` — identical widgets to the parent session. Streaming assistant text **mutates in place** via `updateContent()`, so no duplicate-prefix lines appear as tokens stream in. Tool calls render with expandable output and edit-diff widgets. Implemented via: a new `core/agents/live-sessions.ts` module-level registry (`registerLiveSession`/`unregisterLiveSession`/`getLiveSession`); `executor.ts` registers the child session before driving the prompt loop and deregisters in the `finally` block; `ZoomedSessionTranscript` component in `components/zoomed-session-transcript.ts` subscribes to the session on construction and disposes cleanly; `ZoomedTaskComponent` uses the transcript when a live session is available and falls back to the Phase 1 `TaskMessageEvent` tail for terminal/replay tasks. Parent session settings (cwd, `hideThinkingBlock`, markdown theme, image options) are passed via `ZoomedSessionConfig`. Inject + auto-pop behaviour is unchanged. New test: `zoomed-session-transcript.test.ts` (5 cases: in-place text mutation, tool widget lifecycle, dispose/unsubscribe, registry round-trip, undefined for missing session).
- **Phase 2a** — Footer pill navigation for the TUI zoom view. Pressing `up` on an empty editor with ≥1 running background agent enters footer-nav mode: each running agent is shown as a pill in the footer status line, with the selected pill highlighted in accent bold. `up`/`down` cycle through running agents (wrap-around), `enter` zooms into the selected agent, `escape` cancels without zooming. Keybindings registered as `app.agents.footer.focusPrev` (default `up`), `app.agents.footer.focusNext` (default `down`), `app.agents.footer.zoom` (default `enter`) in `DEFAULT_APP_KEYBINDINGS`. Fall-through to normal editor behaviour when editor is non-empty or no running tasks exist. Implemented via a new `onPreInput` hook on `CustomEditor` that runs before extension shortcuts. Footer selection clears automatically on text input and on escape. The `alt+z` power-user shortcut (`app.agents.zoom.enter`) is preserved. Works in terminals without option-as-alt (e.g. Rusty Warp) because defaults use plain arrow keys. New test: `interactive-mode-footer-nav.test.ts` (8 cases covering focus-prev/next, wrap-around, clear-on-text, propagation to footer component, zoom on enter, no-op with no running tasks).
- Added a TUI zoom-into-running-agent view. Pressing `app.agents.zoom.enter` (default `alt+z`) swaps the main chat pane for a `ZoomedTaskComponent` that renders the live tail of `TaskMessageEvent`s for the most recent running background agent. While zoomed, Enter routes to `LocalAgentTask.injectMessage(taskId, text)` instead of the parent session and emits an immediate `user_injected` event so the operator sees confirmation before the child picks the message up at its next turn. `app.agents.zoom.cycleNext`/`cyclePrev` (default `alt+l`/`alt+h`) walk the shared `getRunningTasksSorted()` order — the same canonical sort used by the footer pill, mirroring Claude Code's `getRunningTeammatesSorted` invariant. `app.agents.zoom.requestShutdown` (default `alt+i`) and `app.agents.zoom.kill` (default `alt+k`) call `LocalAgentTask.requestShutdown` / `kill`. When the zoomed task reaches a terminal status (`completed | failed | cancelled | killed`) the view auto-pops after `STOPPED_DISPLAY_MS` (3s) via a `subscribeAgentRecentRuns` listener + `isTerminalTaskStatus` check. New `core/tasks/sort.ts` exposes `getRunningTasksSorted()` and `cycleRunningTask()`. All keybindings live in `DEFAULT_APP_KEYBINDINGS` (no hardcoded `matchesKey` literals). Regression coverage: `tasks-sort.test.ts` (helper) and `interactive-mode-zoom.test.ts` (component + integration) — plus a tmux smoke script at `packages/coding-agent/test/tmux/zoom-smoke.sh` for end-to-end TTY verification (gated outside vitest because it needs a real provider).
- Added push-based background-agent completion notifications. When a background `agent` run (or `ctx.forkAgent`) reaches a terminal status (`completed | failed | cancelled | interrupted`), the parent session is sent an `agent_completion` custom message carrying `runId`, `status`, `summary`, `result` preview, `output_path`s, `session_path`s, `duration_ms`, `total_tokens`, and `tool_calls`. Mirrors Claude Code's `<task_notification>` shape. The notification fires exactly once per run (atomic dedup via a per-run `notified` flag inside `agents/status.ts`) and is delivered as a `followUp`, so `message_start` fires when the loop picks it up — which is exactly the wake signal pi-goal's `goal_wait` listens for. The `agent` tool's prompt guidelines now explicitly say "do not poll with action=status/detail while waiting”, matching Claude Code's anti-polling rule. New extension hook point: `AgentToolOptions.onBackgroundTerminal(notification)` and `AgentExecutorOptions.onBackgroundTerminal`, wired into the session's `sendCustomMessage` path.
- Added `ctx.forkAgent(opts)` to `ExtensionContext`: spawns a cache-preserving background child agent in `context: "fork"` mode, inheriting the parent's frozen turn-start system prompt 1:1 (byte-identical system + tools prefix for cache hits). Returns `{ handle, sessionId }` where `handle.wait()` resolves with the run's terminal `AgentToolDetails`, `handle.abort()` cancels within ~1s, and `handle.status` snapshots the current `AgentToolStatus`. Caller signal is chained via `cancelAgentRecentRun(runId)`.
- Added `ctx.transcript.append(entry)` to `ExtensionContext` with `TranscriptEntry = { kind: "memory_saved"; verb: "Saved" | "Improved"; paths: string[] }`. Routes through `sendCustomMessage` with `customType: "memory_saved"` so the entry serializes through every mode (interactive renders inline, print/RPC see it in the event stream).
- Added a built-in `memory_saved` message renderer in the interactive TUI (`MemorySavedMessageComponent`). Extension-registered renderers still win; the built-in is a fallback so extensions can append memory entries without shipping their own renderer.
- Added a `"fast"` model alias for the built-in `agent` tool, resolving to the parent provider's mapped cheap variant (Anthropic→Haiku, OpenAI→gpt-5.4-mini, Google→Flash Lite, claude-bridge→Haiku, etc.) via `fastModelPerProvider` in `model-resolver.ts`. Falls back to the parent model when the provider has no mapping. The built-in `explore` agent now defaults to `model: "fast"` so codebase research no longer burns the parent's expensive model.
- Added native background lifecycle control for the built-in `agent` tool, including background launch, footer visibility, selectable `/agents runs` controls, `/agents-status` visibility, interrupt/cancel, and single-run resume.
- Added `pi-agent-tool/eval-design-prompt.md` to design a token-efficient A/B eval comparing native Pi agents with `pi-subagents`.
- Added a native built-in `agent` tool with single, parallel, and chain modes, built-in child agent definitions, user/project Markdown discovery, context modes, `/agents`, and migration docs for the legacy `subagent` extension example.
- Added native-search backend selection for the built-in `grep` and `find` tools, preferring controlled/system `ugrep` and `bfs` before falling back to managed/system `rg` and `fd`.
- Documented Claude Code native search-tool findings and the planned `ugrep`/`bfs` backend direction for Pi's built-in `grep` and `find` tools.

### Changed

- Compact skill listings in the system prompt by rendering each skill as a single XML element and capping prompt descriptions, reducing loaded skill prompt text while preserving names and load paths.
- Tightened the built-in `explore` agent prompt to mirror Claude Code's read-only search specialist: explicit READ-ONLY prohibitions, parallel-tool guidance, caller-specified thoroughness levels (`quick` / `medium` / `very thorough`).
- Removed the built-in `scout` agent; it overlapped `explore`. `explore` is now the single read-only research agent.
- Updated the `agent` tool's prompt guidelines to route codebase research and file/symbol lookups to `explore` instead of `general`, and to prefer `plan` before delegating implementation to `worker`.
- Deferred the built-in `statusline-setup` agent until Pi's statusline target is defined.

### Fixed

- Made the built-in TUI footer context count use an extension-owned cached snapshot that includes the effective system prompt, active provider tool schemas, and transcript/provider usage. Provider tool schemas are top-level request `tools`, not system-prompt text, but still count against the context window; deferred tool index text counts only as prompt text until the full tool schema is active.
- Resolved Anthropic `stop_reason: "pause_turn"` **in-stream** inside `streamAnthropic` instead of mapping it to a terminal `"stop"` (`packages/ai/src/providers/anthropic.ts`). When a long-running server-side tool (`web_search` / `web_fetch` / `code_execution`) needs another turn to finish, Anthropic returns a partial assistant message and the client must echo it back unmodified to resume. The previous mapping let the partial turn reach the agent loop, which persisted it to the session JSONL. On the next user prompt or auto-compaction the partial turn replayed as the latest assistant message and any byte-level drift in a thinking signature triggered a hard 400 (`messages.N.content.M: \"thinking\" or \"redacted_thinking\" blocks in the latest assistant message cannot be modified`) that then poisoned every subsequent request, including compaction. Fix: capture the raw stop reason in `message_delta`, and while it's `pause_turn` (capped at 16 resumes) append the partial assistant message to `context.messages` and re-issue `client.messages.create` with the same `options.onPayload` hook and `requestOptions`. Signed thinking blocks round-trip byte-for-byte through the existing `transformMessages` + assistant-block builder path (`packages/ai/src/providers/anthropic.ts:~1163`), so the resumed request passes Anthropic's signature validation. The `mapStopReason("pause_turn")` arm stays as a defensive fallback (`"stop"`) for any caller wiring `mapStopReason` directly. Regression coverage: `packages/ai/test/anthropic-pause-turn-resume.test.ts` (single-resume happy path with thinking-signature preservation in the continuation payload; multi-resume loop walking three `pause_turn` responses before terminating; resume-limit cap surfacing an `"error"` stop reason with a clear message). (#thinking-roundtrip)
- Documented the **OpenClaw + pi-harness model-namespace ambiguity trap** in [`docs/openclaw-pi-harness-debug.md`](docs/openclaw-pi-harness-debug.md). When OpenClaw registers a custom agentRuntime against an invented prefix (`pi-fork/claude-sonnet-4-6`) instead of the real provider namespace (`claude-bridge/claude-sonnet-4-6`), `session-binding.ts` strips its own provider before spawning pi, leaving pi to resolve a bare `--model claude-sonnet-4-6` against an ambiguous registry (built-in `anthropic/...` vs custom `claude-bridge/...`). Pi defaults to the built-in `anthropic` entry, whose `baseUrl` is hardcoded to `https://api.anthropic.com` in `packages/ai/src/providers/anthropic.ts` (overrides `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL` env), and traffic skips the local OAuth bridge entirely — surfacing as a misleading `"You're out of extra usage"` 400 even when the Max plan is healthy. Doc captures the canonical fix (register the runtime against the underlying provider namespace), a triage runbook, and the bridge `/status` counter as ground-truth diagnostic for "did pi actually go through the bridge?". Reference fix: bermont-kube PR #60.
- Fixed zoomed background-agent pane input semantics. Extension main panes can now handle `Escape` before core falls back to hiding the pane; `pi-agent-ui` uses this so `Esc` interrupts the zoomed agent while `alt+z` or `/exit-zoom` exits zoom. Text entered while zoomed now queues into the live child `AgentSession` via `steer()` for running background agents, falling back to resume-with-prompt only for already-interrupted resumable runs. The zoom UI also shows explicit queued/error status for submitted input. Known limitation: zoom input queues agent messages; it does not write stdin into an active bash tool process.
- Improved interactive responsiveness under frequent render/status updates by scheduling TUI renders with `setImmediate` instead of `process.nextTick`, and caching footer cumulative usage totals between session-entry changes.
- Included the built-in `grep`, `find`, `ls`, and `agent` tools in the default active tool set so the system prompt exposes them when no explicit tool allowlist is configured.
- Added bounded default timeouts to the built-in `grep` and `find` tools with structured timeout results, partial output when available, AbortSignal preservation, and explicit `timeout` overrides up to 300 seconds.
- Fixed runtime active-tool changes made during tool execution so the next provider request in the same agent run receives the refreshed tool schema. This makes deferred-tool activators such as `tool_search` able to expose newly activated tools immediately, and deduplicates repeated active tool names.

### Removed

- Removed the fork-retained `packages/web-ui` workspace after upstream deleted it and local audit confirmed zero live consumers. Also removed the stale web-ui references from `tsconfig.json` and the pre-commit browser-smoke trigger.

## 2026-05-02

- Locally aliased the installed `pi-subagents` manager command from `/agents` to `/subagents` for A/B testing against native `/agents`; this lives under `~/.pi/agent/git/github.com/nicobailon/pi-subagents` and may be overwritten by `pi update`.
- Merged upstream `v0.72.0` into the fork.

    36	- **Slimmed the upstream-owned package changelogs (400KB → stubs) and flipped them to fork-owned `merge=ours`.** The package `CHANGELOG.md` files carried `earendil-works/pi-mono`'s full Keep-a-Changelog history and grew unbounded because `.gitattributes` `*CHANGELOG.md merge=union` made every sync *append* (never replace) — `coding-agent` reached 407KB. Archived each `packages/*/CHANGELOG.md` → `CHANGELOG.upstream.md` (frozen reference, full history preserved), reset `CHANGELOG.md` to a fork-owned stub pointing at `FORK-CHANGELOG.md` + the archive, and changed `.gitattributes`: `packages/*/CHANGELOG.md merge=ours` (fork keeps its stub across syncs — no re-bloat) with the `.upstream.md` archives staying `merge=union`. Changesets stays `changelog: false` (it never wrote these). This is the deliberate ownership change deferred from the release hotfix; the release-side bounded-body fix (`createGithubReleases:false` + `create-github-releases.mjs`) already keeps publishing safe and is unaffected. See `docs/adr/0002-slim-upstream-changelogs.md`.
    37	- **Generated model registries decoupled from `build` + `merge=ours` to stop recurring sync conflicts and dirty trees.** `packages/ai/src/{models,image-models}.generated.ts` are generated from **live** provider API fetches (`generate-models.ts` does `await fetch()` against OpenRouter, NVIDIA NIM, …), so their contents depend on what each registry publishes at build time — upstream's committed snapshot and the fork's never match, hard-conflicting on every sync, and every `build:binary` re-fetched and re-wrote them, leaving the tree dirty. Two coordinated changes: (1) `packages/ai` `build` no longer runs `generate-models`/`generate-image-models` (now just `tsgo -p tsconfig.build.json`); generation moved to an explicit `npm --prefix packages/ai run refresh-models` you invoke deliberately — builds compile the committed snapshot and no longer touch it. (2) `.gitattributes` `packages/ai/src/{models,image-models}.generated.ts merge=ours` so upstream's churn in these files auto-resolves to the fork's snapshot on merge; the `ours` driver is registered per-clone by `scripts/setup-merge-drivers.sh` (run once). No `--check` gate added on purpose — the data is live/non-deterministic, so a strict check would flake whenever a provider tweaks a value. Trade-off: the committed snapshot goes stale between manual refreshes (acceptable — `refresh-models` re-fetches everything live on demand). Logged in `my-pi/docs/pi-fork-patch-inventory.md`.
    38	- **Changelog ownership split to stop recurring upstream-sync conflicts.** Package `CHANGELOG.md` files are now strictly upstream-owned (Keep-a-Changelog style, fast-forwarded from upstream); all fork-specific notes live here in `FORK-CHANGELOG.md`. Three coordinated changes: (1) `.changeset/config.json` `changelog: false` so changesets stops writing fork entries into package CHANGELOGs (it still versions packages); (2) `scripts/check-changelog-updated.mjs` now accepts a touched `FORK-CHANGELOG.md` as satisfying the changelog requirement for package-src changes (package CHANGELOGs may still be updated directly for upstreamable work, but are no longer mandatory); (3) `.gitattributes` `*CHANGELOG.md merge=union` as a safety net so a stray package-CHANGELOG edit auto-unions on the next sync instead of hard-conflicting. Root cause: changesets and upstream's manual changelog both wrote the top of the same files in different formats, hard-conflicting on every sync.
    39	- **Upstream 0.79.0 sync (merge `ee822529`): synced `earendil-works/pi-mono` v0.79.0 into the fork.** 15 conflicts resolved mechanically (changelogs, 4× `package.json` exact-pinned to `@valkyriweb@0.79.0`, loader signature, widget imports). The recurring `resource-loader.ts` seam resolved via the hook/filter approach — adopted 0.79.0's project-trust methods and threaded the three fork features cleanly: F1 deferred extensions (`ExtensionLoadRequest[]` + `deferredExtensions`), F2 post-trust `extensionConfig` (trusted/merged config), F3 hooks via the existing `load` hook seam (`loadExtensionHooks` consumed in `loadFinalExtensionSet`). Additive conflicts (interactive-mode, runner test) kept both sides. Lockfile + shrinkwrap regenerated to 0.79.0; `models.generated.ts` / `image-models.generated.ts` regenerated from models.dev at build time (build output). Full build + `test:build-gate` green (system-prompt, cache-stability 38, e2e 184, full my-pi extension gate). `AGENTS.md` gained an extensibility ladder (existing hook/filter → new upstreamable hook/filter → inline patch as last resort).
    40	- **Consolidation pass (PR #58): synced `upstream/main` (52 commits, through v0.78.1) and landed open fork PRs #57/#55/#23 in one branch.** Upstream brings the TUI overlay-focus fixes (PR #5235 / issue #5129) that make focused interactive overlays receive Enter again — fixing the idle-return modal that ignored Enter and only closed on Esc — plus project-trust gating, system-prompt-options for extension commands, NVIDIA NIM / ZAI / Ant Ling / MiniMax providers, `httpIdleTimeoutMs` for all providers, and a Bedrock blank-text fix. Conflict resolutions preserved fork behavior over upstream where they overlapped: claude-bridge routing in `sdk.ts` now threads through upstream's `mergeProviderAttributionHeaders`; `footer.ts` keeps the fork's richer `cache X% avg Y%` panel over upstream's `CH%`; `interactive-mode.ts` unions upstream `showTrustSelector` with the fork's agent selectors and keeps the `footerInputUnsubscribe` cleanup; `resource-loader.ts` keeps the fork `@`-import expansion under upstream's `projectTrusted` gate. Two upstream-new files (`provider-attribution.ts`, `trust-selector.ts`) rescoped from `@earendil-works/*` to `@valkyriweb/*`; model catalogs + lockfiles regenerated; upstream's new system-prompt-options test adapted to the fork's CC-capitalized tool names. PR #44 (canary comment only) intentionally not merged. Landed work: #57 interactive runtime footers, #55 mid-run compaction cap + work-counter placement, #23 generative-UI/build-interface tools.

    45	### Fixed
    46	
    47	- **Background bash jobs now wake the agent on completion (`#bash-bg-completion-wake`) — the documented notification was never wired for bash.** A `run_in_background:true` bash command ran, completed, updated the TUI footer via `notifyBashBgJobsChanged()`, and pushed **nothing** to the model. Only background *agent* runs had a wake path (`onBackgroundTerminal` → `AgentSession._emitAgentCompletion` → `sendCustomMessage`); the bash tool description still inherited Claude Code's promise ("you'll be notified when it finishes") and `core/tools/background-tasks.ts` even documented "Output is push-notified on completion", but the bash side of that wiring never existed. Net effect: a CC-trained model narrated "they'll wake me when done" and parked forever on a wake that never came. Fix mirrors the agent path: a `subscribeBashBgTerminal` listener registry in `core/tools/bash.ts` fires once on **natural** termination only (process exit / spawn error — explicit `bash_kill`, `killAll`, and session dispose deliberately do **not** fire, since the agent already knows it stopped them); `AgentSession.emitBashCompletion(job)` builds a `<task_notification>` custom message (task id, status, exit code, command, elapsed, output log path) and delivers it via `deliverAs: "followUp"` exactly like `_emitAgentCompletion`; the single **main interactive session** wires the subscription in `interactive-mode.ts` (the bg-bash store is process-global, so subscribing here rather than in every forked child session avoids duplicate notifications). The bash tool description + guideline were reworded to truthfully promise the wake and tell the model not to poll or re-run to "check" (one-time `tools[]` cache re-warm, then stable). Regression: `test/bash-background.test.ts` (natural-exit fires once with `status: exited`/`exit 0`; explicit kill fires zero times). Logged in `my-pi/docs/pi-fork-patch-inventory.md`.
    48	- **Release publish no longer 422s on the upstream changelog size ("body is too long").** The `Release` workflow used `changesets/action`'s default `createGithubReleases: true`, which builds each package's GitHub Release body by matching a heading whose text equals the version (`## 0.31.0`). The fork's package `CHANGELOG.md` files are upstream-owned Keep-a-Changelog (`## [0.31.0] - 2026-01-02`, `coding-agent` is 400KB+ via `merge=union`), so the match always fails and the action falls back to dumping the **entire file** as the body — exceeding GitHub's 125000-char Release-body cap → `422` → the whole publish job reds (sometimes after publishing to the registry but before every Release is cut). Set `createGithubReleases: false` and added `.github/scripts/create-github-releases.mjs`, a post-publish step that cuts a Release per just-published package (from `steps.changesets.outputs.publishedPackages`) with a small, bounded body pointing at `FORK-CHANGELOG.md` — never the upstream changelog. The upstream-owned changelogs and `merge=union` are left untouched (slimming them is deferred to a separate ownership change with its own ADR). Idempotent (skips packages that already have a Release). Mirrors the same fix in the `my-pi` repo (#139).
    49	- **`biome check` no longer breaks on stray local Pi workspaces.** `.pi/workspaces/` is gitignored globally but not in the repo `.gitignore`, and Biome's `vcs.useIgnoreFile` only reads the repo-local ignore — so a leftover workspace (e.g. `.pi/workspaces/upstream-tti/biome.json` from an upstream-sync session) was discovered as a nested root config and aborted `npm run check` repo-wide. Added `.pi/workspaces/` to the repo `.gitignore` so Biome skips it for everyone (matching the existing `.pi/workflows/` entry).
    50	- **Extension loader resolves upstream package names (`@earendil-works/*`, `@mariozechner/*`).** The fork renamed its packages to `@valkyriweb/*`, but third-party extensions in the ecosystem still import the upstream scopes — `@earendil-works/*` (current upstream) and `@mariozechner/*` (legacy). Type-only imports erase at runtime, but extensions with **value** imports (e.g. pi-autoresearch pulling `truncateTail`/`formatSize`/`StringEnum`/`Text` as runtime values) failed to load with `Cannot find module "@mariozechner/pi-coding-agent"`. Added compatibility entries for both upstream scopes mapping onto the same fork modules, in **both** resolution paths: `getAliases()` (jiti, Node/dev mode) and `VIRTUAL_MODULES` (the compiled Bun binary that live `pi` actually runs — line 682 selects `virtualModules` over `alias` when `isBunBinary`). Covers `pi-coding-agent`, `pi-agent-core`, `pi-tui`, `pi-ai`, and `pi-ai/oauth`. Generic platform compatibility primitive (extension module resolution) that can't be expressed through hooks — restores the third-party extension ecosystem on the fork without each extension needing a `@valkyriweb/*` rewrite.
    51	- **`setActiveToolsByName` cache-burst no-op guard (cache law #4).** Before rewriting `agent.state.tools` and rebuilding the system prompt, the method now early-returns when the freshly built `tools[]` is element-for-element **reference-identical** to the current state. An unconditional refresh on every `tools_changed`/`_refreshToolRegistry` event bursts the within-session `tools[]` (and system-prompt) cache prefix even when nothing actually changed. Reference-equality (not name-set equality) is the correct test: pi rebuilds the registry with fresh object refs whenever a definition changes (a tool gains `deferLoading`, an allowlist empties), so a genuine change yields different refs and the rebuild proceeds — only a true no-op early-returns (mirrors pi-ai's `convertedToolCache` WeakMap keyed by tool reference). Guard is skipped until the base prompt has been built once (`_baseSystemPromptOptions` is set only by `_rebuildSystemPrompt`), so the cold init `empty→empty` rebuild still runs. Same change adds the post-registration **deferral-override seam** (`setDeferredToolOverrides`/`_applyDeferredOverrides`): extensions can force already-registered tools to `deferLoading:true` so they ride `tools[]` as `defer_loading` stubs across every registry rebuild, with the same unchanged-set no-op guard (`sameStringSet`) so a redundant call doesn't burst the prefix. Also threads the live agent state into `createPromptCacheAffinityKey` on every model switch so the affinity key tracks the actual model rather than a stale cwd-only key.
    52	- **Changelog guard: package-level test-only changes no longer wrongly require a CHANGELOG.** `requiredChangelog()` in `scripts/check-changelog-updated.mjs` returned the package `CHANGELOG.md` for any `packages/<pkg>/` path before consulting `isIgnored()` (which already covers test-only paths via `isTestOnly()`), so a change touching only `packages/<pkg>/test/**` failed the guard, contradicting the script's own "tests-only ... are ignored" message and the AGENTS changelog rules. Now `isIgnored(path)` is checked first (returns no requirement), then package/fork resolution. Verified with crafted diffs: a package test-only change passes, a package src change without its CHANGELOG still fails.
    53	- **Workflow shellcheck hygiene: quoted `$(which fdfind)` and grouped `$GITHUB_OUTPUT` redirects so `actionlint` (incl. shellcheck) is clean.** SC2046 (word-splitting on unquoted command substitution) in `ci.yml`, `build-binaries.yml`, and `release.yml`; SC2129 (consecutive redirects) in the `upstream-sync.yml` conflict branch. Because `packages/tui` had not been built yet, the gate crashed with `Cannot find package '.../@valkyriweb/pi-tui/dist/index.js'`, failing the `Build workspace declarations` step on every PR. New order: `tui → ai → agent → coding-agent`, then `test:build-gate` last, so the gate runs against freshly built dist (its intent — catching prompt-cache/system-prompt regressions before a build ships — is unchanged). The guard runs the extension gate locally (where `../my-pi` exists) and skips with a notice on CI. Dirty local work:

## Contract

- Treat review output as advisory. Never blindly apply it.
- Verify every finding by reading the real code path and adjacent files.
- Read dependency docs/source/types when the finding depends on external behavior.
- Reject unrealistic edge cases, speculative risks, broad rewrites, and fixes that over-complicate the codebase.
- Prefer small fixes at the right ownership boundary; no refactor unless it clearly improves the bug class.
- Keep going until structured review returns no accepted/actionable findings.
- If a review-triggered fix changes code, rerun focused tests and rerun the structured review helper.
- For security-audit suppression changes, verify accepted findings remain auditable: suppressed findings stay in structured output, active output keeps an unsuppressible suppression notice, and aggregate findings cannot hide unrelated active risk.
- Never switch or override the requested review engine/model. If the review hits model capacity, retry the same command a few times with the same engine/model.
- Be patient with large bundles. Structured review can be silent for several minutes while the model call is active, especially with Codex tools or web search. Treat `review still running: ... elapsed=... pid=...` as healthy progress, not a hang.
- Do not kill a review just because it has been quiet for 2-5 minutes. Inspect the process only after multiple heartbeat intervals or an obviously failed subprocess; prefer letting the same helper command finish.
- Tools are useful in review mode. The helper allows read-only inspection tools and web search by default so reviewers can check dependency contracts, upstream docs, and current behavior.
- Security perspective is always included, but it should not cripple legitimate functionality. Report security findings only when the change creates a concrete, actionable risk or removes an important safety check.
- For regression provenance, if no blamed PR is traceable, use the blamed commit as the provenance: commit SHA, date, and author username. Do not guess a merger or frame missing PR metadata as a separate finding.
- Do not invoke built-in `codex review`, nested reviewers, or reviewer panels from inside the review. The helper builds one bundle, calls one selected engine, validates one structured result, and stops.
- Stop as soon as the helper exits 0 with no accepted/actionable findings. Do not run an extra review just to get a nicer "clean" line, a second opinion, or clearer closeout wording.
- Treat the helper's successful exit plus absence of actionable findings as the clean review result, even if the underlying Codex CLI output is terse.
- Multi-reviewer panels are opt-in only. Use them when explicitly requested or when risk justifies the extra spend; the main agent still verifies every accepted finding before fixing.
- If rejecting a finding as intentional/not worth fixing, add a brief inline code comment only when it explains a real invariant or ownership decision that future reviewers should know.
- If `gh`/Gitcrawl reports `database disk image is malformed`, run `gitcrawl doctor --json` once to let the portable cache repair before retrying review; do not bypass the shim unless repair fails and freshness requires live GitHub.

Run multiple reviewers against one frozen bundle:

<autoreview-helper> --reviewers codex,claude

File-based handoffs live in `./.go-output/`. The arc mirrors a manual ship cycle — clean up the diff, verify it works (surfacing regressions the request didn't ask about), get an independent review, open the PR, then watch CI and fix failures as they land — so the human can hand off the whole loop, not just the build.

## References

| Phase | Handoff template |
|---|---|
| 1 Verify | `references/phase-1-verify.md` |
| 2 Code Review | `references/phase-2-code-review.md` |
| 3 Review gate | `references/phase-3-code-craft.md`; non-trivial fan-out also uses `references/phase-3-security.md` and `references/phase-3-test-engineer.md`; UI changes also use `references/phase-3-design.md` |
| 4 PR | `references/phase-4-pr.md` |
| 5 CI watch | `references/phase-5-ci-watch.md` |

Each handoff is self-contained: the subagent gets the file's contents (with `{{CWD}}` interpolated), reads the artifacts from prior phases, and returns a single-line STATUS.

## File workspace

```
.go-output/
  context.md      # Phase 0 writes — scope, classification, commands
  verify.md       # Phase 1 writes
  slop-scan.md    # Phase 1 writes when slop-scan is available (advisory)
  verify-*.png    # Phase 1 writes (screenshots)
  code-review.md  # Phase 2 writes
  code-craft.md   # Phase 3 writes (## Fixed + ## Follow-ups)
  security.md     # Phase 3 fan-out writes when security review runs
  test-review.md  # Phase 3 fan-out writes when test review runs
  design.md       # Phase 3 fan-out writes when the diff touched UI
  review-gate.md  # Phase 3 synthesis writes
  pr.md           # Phase 4 writes (PR URL + commits)
  ci-watch.md     # Phase 5 writes (CI result + any autofix commits)
```

Create the directory in Phase 0 and add `.go-output/` to `.gitignore` if absent — these are ephemeral.

## Phase 0 — Orchestrator setup

1. Capture scope:
   ```bash
   git status --porcelain
   git diff --stat
   # If tree is clean and commits exist on a branch:
   base=$(git merge-base HEAD origin/main 2>/dev/null || git merge-base HEAD main)
   git log --oneline "$base"..HEAD
   git diff --stat "$base"..HEAD
   ```
2. **Detect unrelated changes.** Compare the modified files against the user's stated work. Any file that doesn't fit the intent (e.g. `scripts/debug.py` when the user is shipping `feat/csv-export`) is unrelated. If unrelated changes exist, halt before writing `context.md` and surface three options to the user: commit them on the current branch, stash them, or move them to a separate branch. 3. Classify the change as one or more of: `backend-cli`, `web-ui`, `desktop-native`, `refactor`.

Set `yes` only if the diff changes a rendered UI surface: components/templates/markup (`.tsx/.jsx/.vue/.svelte/.astro/.html/.blade.php`), styles (`.css/.scss/.less`, Tailwind classes), or design tokens. # How I Work

Bias: caution over speed; for trivial tasks use judgment.

## Think Before Coding
- State assumptions explicitly; uncertain → ask. Multiple interpretations → present them, don't pick silently.
- Simpler approach exists → say so; push back when warranted. Confused → stop, name it, ask.

## Simplicity First
- Minimum code that solves the problem; nothing speculative: no features beyond the ask, no abstractions for single-use code, no unrequested configurability, no error handling for impossible scenarios.
- 200 lines that could be 50 → rewrite. Test: would a senior engineer call this overcomplicated?

## Surgical Changes
- Reuse existing types/utilities/patterns before writing new ones; don't broaden public APIs unless required.
- Don't improve adjacent code/comments/formatting; match existing style. Unrelated dead code → mention, don't delete.
- Quality blocking the task → improve it as part of the change, call it out. Real issue outside the task → flag, don't expand scope.
- Remove orphans YOUR change created; leave pre-existing ones. Every changed line traces to the request.

## Goal-Driven Execution
- Verifiable goals: "fix the bug" → "test that reproduces it, make it pass". Multi-step → brief plan, one verify per step.
- Spec work: slices traceable to spec/issue; "what's left?" = concrete file/task deltas; checkpoint before risky refactors.
- Don't fight errors: same error twice → stop, gather evidence (local docs/source first, then web) before the next fix.

- `docs/pi-stack-inventory.md` — **runtime deployments** (every place pi + claude-bridge runs across the fleet, with request-flow diagram), plus repos/packages/extensions/eval surfaces. Start here for any "where does pi run?" question.
- `docs/pi-organization-boundaries.md` — target layout, overlap matrix, and migration phases.
- `docs/pi-decisions.md` — timestamped architecture/boundary decisions.
- `docs/tasks.md` — active task list.
- `docs/goals/goal-2026-05-30T07-50-47Z-pi-platform-program.md` — **active platform program**: release engineering (versioned `@valkyriweb` registry + Changesets), config layering (`extensionConfig`/`getExtensionConfig`, L1–L4), Effect adoption, PR review gates (`pr-pipeline-orchestrator` chain), and blocking cache/prompt-stability release acceptance. New refs: `docs/release-engineering.md`, `docs/config-layering.md`.

## Session Briefing Card

`~/obsidian/dream-memory/memory/profile/00-pi-active-context.md` — compact (≤1500 tok) briefing card injected on every session start via dream-memory harness. Covers: claude-bridge provider config, active projects, pi extensions, openclaw separation, active-memory/dreaming behaviour.

- Named `00-` → loads first in lex-sort, guaranteed within the 8-file cap.
- Keep under 6 kB. Update when project focus or runtime config changes.
- Do not add timestamps or session-specific content (breaks LLM cache).
- Format: stable markdown tables and bullets — no counters, no dates.

## Pi Context Block (session-start memory)

`~/obsidian/dream-memory/memory/profile/MEMORY.md` is the single file auto-injected every session (≤1500 tokens, cache-stable). It contains:
- **Preferences & Policies** (refs to detail files)
- **Infrastructure** notes
- **Pi Stack** — fork, extensions, packages, claude-bridge, active-memory, dream
- **Active Projects & OpenClaw** — high-traffic repos + openclaw env separation

Dream upserts individual H2 sections when relevant events accumulate. Manual updates are fine; keep the file under ~5.8 kB to stay within the token budget. Regenerate the Active Projects section when the project mix shifts significantly.

## pi-memory extraction

Per-turn `turn_end` extraction (CC `extractMemories` parity); consolidation cadence belongs to dream-memory. Before touching extraction gating, env vars, or the dream boundary, read `docs/memory-extraction-parity.md`.

## Pi Change Workflow

Use this before modifying `my-pi` or `pi-mono-fork`:

1. Read the local Pi docs above for the touched surface.
2. Choose extension/package first; if core is unavoidable, climb the extensibility ladder (existing hook/filter → new upstreamable hook/filter → inline patch as last resort) and write a short note justifying the chosen rung.
3. Run Matt Pocock's architecture review lens: `~/Projects/agent-scripts/skills/matt-pocock/references/improve-codebase-architecture.md`.
4. For broad changes, anchor slices to the relevant spec/goal doc and report concrete remaining deltas.
5. Make one incremental simplification when it is local, safe, and directly adjacent to the change.
6. Update `docs/pi-setup/catalog/*.yaml` and governed docs for setup/runtime changes; never hand-edit `docs/pi-setup/generated/`.

## Subagent routing

When spawning agents from Workflow scripts, `Agent`, or extension-owned forks, read `docs/agent-routing.md` for the alias/model/thinking matrix. Default: explicit cheap routing (`explore`+`fast` for read-only fan-out) over inherited expensive defaults.

## Cache Stability (mandatory for fork + extension work)

Any change touching `forkAgent`, child agents, system-prompt construction, or background extractors **must** review the `pi-cache-stability` skill first. Anthropic prompt cache only helps when the prefix is byte-identical and alive within TTL — pi forks and extensions break this constantly without realising. The skill captures the L1/L2/L3 levers (`context: "slim"|"none"`, `systemPrompt` override, `BRIDGE_CACHE_TTL=1h`), the audit checklist, and the verification recipe. Source-of-truth doc: `docs/cache-strategy.md`.

## Pre-PR local review

**PR gate (run order):** `codex-review` → `code-craft-pr` → `matt-pocock/improve-codebase-architecture` → `docs-freshness-pr` (wire through `pr-pipeline-orchestrator`); resolve all Tier 1/2 findings and file Tier 3 as GitHub issues. Before opening/updating/declaring a PR ready, read `docs/review-guidelines.md` for the review lenses, P1 flag list, agent-ci command, and the ClawSweeper autonomous lane. Stop before PR on a real P1 — fix it or document the deferral.

Before changing runtime extension behavior, run the relevant eval or add one if none exists.

- When installing, adding, modifying, or removing Pi extensions/packages, run the my-pi extension checks and the fork cache gate together:

name: autofix-pr
description: "Drive a pull request to green: gather failing CI + unresolved review threads, fix locally, gate, push, reply, loop till clean. Triggers: 'autofix this PR', 'fix the failing CI', 'address review comments', 'get PR #N green'."
---

# autofix-pr

Local-first parity for Claude Code's remote `autofix-pr` monitor. CC runs it as a
cloud remote-agent that watches a PR and emits a result per notification cycle;
here you run the same loop locally with `gh` and the repo's own gate.

Use when asked to fix a PR's failing checks or address its review feedback —
not for opening a fresh PR (that's `/go`).

## Preconditions

- `gh repo view --json viewerPermission` shows write (`ADMIN`/`MAINTAIN`/`WRITE`).
  No write access → stop, report. Never push to a repo you don't own unless asked.
- Identify the PR: explicit `#N`/URL, else the PR for the current branch
  (`gh pr view --json number,headRefName,state`).
- Branch must be the PR's head branch and clean-ish; if another session shares
  the checkout, use a Git worktree.

## Loop (repeat until clean or blocked)

1. **Gather signals** — one pass, save to `/tmp/autofix-pr-<N>.json`:
   - Failing checks: `gh pr checks <N>` → for each failure, `gh run view <run-id> --log-failed`.
   - Unresolved review threads: `gh pr view <N> --json reviews,comments` (+ GraphQL
     `reviewThreads` for resolved state); collect file/line + ask.
   - Merge conflicts / out-of-date base.
2. **Triage** — classify each signal: lint/format (auto), test failure (reproduce
   first), type error, review change-request, flaky/infra (don't "fix" — note it).
   Cite the concrete artifact (log line, file:line) per item. No artifact → don't guess.
3. **Fix** — surgical, scoped to the signal (see `/code-craft`, HOW-I-WORK surgical
   rule). Add a regression test when a bug fix fits. One logical fix per concern.
4. **Gate** — smallest meaningful local gate before pushing (lint/typecheck/test/build,
   repo's own CI command if it runs locally). Fix-until-green locally first.
5. **Push** — `git push`. Don't force-push shared history; `--force-with-lease` only
   if you own the branch and rebased intentionally.
6. **Reply** — per resolved thread, comment citing the fix + file/line; resolve the
   thread only after the fix has landed (push confirmed). Don't resolve threads you
   didn't fix. (AGENTS.md PR Feedback.)
7. **Re-poll CI** — `gh pr checks <N> --watch` (or re-run step 1) until green.
   Same failure 3× → stop (3-strike rule): report what's fixed, what's stuck, why.

## Stop / escalate

- Flaky or infra failure (not your diff) → re-run once (`gh run rerun --failed`);
  still red → report, don't paper over.
- Review asks for a design change or scope you can't infer → ask one concise question.
- Conflicting reviewer asks → surface both, don't pick silently.

## Report

End with: PR state, checks (green/red list), threads addressed vs open, commits
pushed, and any `[blocked]` item with the specific missing input.

#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail

# Shared auto-compaction threshold for agent harnesses.
if [ -f "$HOME/.pi/agent/token-budget.env" ]; then
  set +u
  . "$HOME/.pi/agent/token-budget.env"
  set -u
  export PI_AUTO_COMPACT_TOKEN_LIMIT CLAUDE_CODE_AUTO_COMPACT_WINDOW
fi

# Source ~/.zshenv to inherit user env (PATH, DREAM_QMD_HTTP_PORT, etc.)
# Warp launches commands via `zsh --no_rcs` which skips all rc files, so Pi
# would otherwise inherit a near-empty environment.
#
# Skip-on-sentinel: when PI_ENV_LOADED=1 is already set, the parent shell
# (or an earlier pi launch in the same shell tree) already sourced it. This
# saves ~60ms on every nested pi launch (intercom-spawned sessions, agent
# subprocesses). Warp/first-launch still pays the cost.
if [ -f "$HOME/.zshenv" ] && [ -z "${PI_ENV_LOADED:-}" ]; then
  set +u
  source "$HOME/.zshenv" 2>/dev/null || true
  set -u
  export PI_ENV_LOADED=1
fi

An app is equivalent to a set of MCP tools within the `codex_apps` MCP.
An installed app's MCP tools are either provided to you already, or can be lazy-loaded through the `tool_search` tool. If `tool_search` is available, the apps that are searchable by `tools_search` will be listed by it.
Do not additionally call list_mcp_resources or list_mcp_resource_templates for apps.
</apps_instructions>

# How I Work

Bias: caution over speed; for trivial tasks use judgment.

## Think Before Coding
- State assumptions explicitly; uncertain → ask. Multiple interpretations → present them, don't pick silently.
- Simpler approach exists → say so; push back when warranted. Confused → stop, name it, ask.

## Simplicity First
- Minimum code that solves the problem; nothing speculative: no features beyond the ask, no abstractions for single-use code, no unrequested configurability, no error handling for impossible scenarios.
- 200 lines that could be 50 → rewrite. Test: would a senior engineer call this overcomplicated?

## Surgical Changes
- Reuse existing types/utilities/patterns before writing new ones; don't broaden public APIs unless required.
- Don't improve adjacent code/comments/formatting; match existing style. Unrelated dead code → mention, don't delete.
- Quality blocking the task → improve it as part of the change, call it out. Real issue outside the task → flag, don't expand scope.
- Remove orphans YOUR change created; leave pre-existing ones. Every changed line traces to the request.

## Goal-Driven Execution
- Verifiable goals: "fix the bug" → "test that reproduces it, make it pass". Multi-step → brief plan, one verify per step.
- Spec work: slices traceable to spec/issue; "what's left?" = concrete file/task deltas; checkpoint before risky refactors.
- Don't fight errors: same error twice → stop, gather evidence (local docs/source first, then web) before the next fix.

# my-pi Agent Instructions

## Priorities

- Keep boot context small; move detail into focused docs under `docs/`.

- Add custom Pi functionality in `my-pi` as an extension or pi package first.
- Reach into `pi-mono-fork` core only via the **extensibility ladder** — stop at the first rung that works:
  1. **Use an existing upstream extension point** — documented SDK/extension APIs and the hook/filter registry (`addAction`/`addFilter`/`registerHook`, `applyFilters`). Check whether upstream already exposes (or even registers-but-doesn't-consume) a hook for the behavior before writing anything.
  2. **Add a new generic, additive hook/filter** to core at a stable call site, then have the fork *consume* it from an extension. Prefer **upstreaming the primitive** to `earendil-works/pi` so the fork eventually carries no patch.
  3. **Inline core-logic patches are the last resort** — they re-conflict on every upstream sync. Never fork the body of a function upstream actively edits when a thin, consumable hook point would do.
- Litmus test: if a fork change would collide with upstream the next time they touch that file, it belongs behind a hook/filter, not inline. Favor small additive seams over forked behavior.
- Add eval coverage for any prompt/context optimization that could affect recall.
- Preserve compatibility with upstream pi where practical.

# Checkout v4

This action checks-out your repository under `$GITHUB_WORKSPACE`, so your workflow can access it.

Only a single commit is fetched by default, for the ref/SHA that triggered the workflow. Set `fetch-depth: 0` to fetch all history for all branches and tags. Refer [here](https://docs.github.com/actions/using-workflows/events-that-trigger-workflows) to learn which commit `$GITHUB_SHA` points to for different events.

The auth token is persisted in the local git config. This enables your scripts to run authenticated git commands. The token is removed during post-job cleanup. Set `persist-credentials: false` to opt-out.

When Git 2.18 or higher is not in your PATH, falls back to the REST API to download the files.

# setup-node

[![basic-validation](https://github.com/actions/setup-node/actions/workflows/basic-validation.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/actions/setup-node/actions/workflows/basic-validation.yml)
[![versions](https://github.com/actions/setup-node/actions/workflows/versions.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/actions/setup-node/actions/workflows/versions.yml)
[![e2e-cache](https://github.com/actions/setup-node/actions/workflows/e2e-cache.yml/badge.svg?branch=main)](https://github.com/actions/setup-node/actions/workflows/e2e-cache.yml)
[![proxy](https://github.com/actions/setup-node/actions/workflows/proxy.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/actions/setup-node/actions/workflows/proxy.yml)

This action provides the following functionality for GitHub Actions users:

- Optionally downloading and caching distribution of the requested Node.js version, and adding it to the PATH
- Optionally caching npm/yarn/pnpm dependencies
- Registering problem matchers for error output
- Configuring authentication for GPR or npm

## Breaking changes in V6

- Caching is now automatically enabled for npm projects when either the `devEngines.packageManager` field or the top-level `packageManager` field in `package.json` is set to `npm`. For other package managers, such as Yarn and pnpm, caching is disabled by default and must be configured manually using the `cache` input.

- The `always-auth` input has been removed, as it is deprecated and will no longer be supported in future npm releases. To ensure your workflows continue to run without warnings or errors, please remove any references to `always-auth` from your configuration.

## Breaking changes in V5

- Enabled caching by default with package manager detection if no cache input is provided.
  > For workflows with elevated privileges or access to sensitive information, we recommend disabling automatic caching by setting `package-manager-cache: false` when caching is not needed for secure operation.

- Upgraded action from node20 to node24.
  > Make sure your runner is on version v2.327.1 or later to ensure compatibility with this release. [See Release Notes](https://github.com/actions/runner/releases/tag/v2.327.1)

For more details, see the full release notes on the [releases page](https://github.com/actions/setup-node/releases/v5.0.0)

## Usage

See [action.yml](action.yml)

<!-- start usage -->
```yaml
- uses: actions/setup-node@v6
  with:
    # Version Spec of the version to use in SemVer notation.
    # It also admits such aliases as lts/*, latest, nightly and canary builds
    # Examples: 12.x, 10.15.1, >=10.15.0, lts/Hydrogen, 16-nightly, latest, node
    node-version: ''

    # File containing the version Spec of the version to use.  Examples: package.json, .nvmrc, .node-version, .tool-versions.
    # If node-version and node-version-file are both provided the action will use version from node-version.
    node-version-file: ''

    # Set this option if you want the action to check for the latest available version
    # that satisfies the version spec.
    # It will only get affect for lts Nodejs versions (12.x, >=10.15.0, lts/Hydrogen).
    # Default: false
    check-latest: false

    # Target architecture for Node to use. Examples: x86, x64. Will use system architecture by default.
    # Default: ''. The action use system architecture by default
    architecture: ''

    # Used to pull node distributions from https://github.com/actions/node-versions.
    # Since there's a default, this is typically not supplied by the user.
    # When running this action on github.com, the default value is sufficient.
    # When running on GHES, you can pass a personal access token for github.com if you are experiencing rate limiting.
    #
    # We recommend using a service account with the least permissions necessary. Also
    # when generating a new PAT, select the least scopes necessary.
    #
    # [Learn more about creating and using encrypted secrets](https://help.github.com/en/actions/automating-your-workflow-with-github-actions/creating-and-using-encrypted-secrets)
    #
    # Default: ${{ github.server_url == 'https://github.com' && github.token || '' }}
    token: ''

    # Used to specify a package manager for caching in the default directory. Supported values: npm, yarn, pnpm.
    # Package manager should be pre-installed
    # Default: ''
    cache: ''

    # Controls automatic caching for npm. By default, caching for npm is enabled if either the devEngines.packageManager field or the top-level packageManager field in package.json specifies npm and no explicit cache input is provided.
    # To disable automatic caching for npm, set package-manager-cache to false.
    # default: true
    package-manager-cache: true

    # Used to specify the path to a dependency file: package-lock.json, yarn.lock, etc.
    # It will generate hash from the target file for primary key. It works only If cache is specified.
    # Supports wildcards or a list of file names for caching multiple dependencies.
    # Default: ''
    cache-dependency-path: ''

    # Optional registry to set up for auth. Will set the registry in a project level .npmrc and .yarnrc file,
    # and set up auth to read in from env.NODE_AUTH_TOKEN.
    # Default: ''
    registry-url: ''

    # Optional scope for authenticating against scoped registries.
    # Will fall back to the repository owner when using the GitHub Packages registry (https://npm.pkg.github.com/).
    # Default: ''
    scope: ''

    # Optional mirror to download binaries from.
    # Artifacts need to match the official Node.js
    # Example:
    # V8 Canary Build: <mirror_url>/download/v8-canary
    # RC Build: <mirror_url>/download/rc
    # Official: Build <mirror_url>/dist
    # Nightly build: <mirror_url>/download/nightly
    # Default: ''
    mirror: ''

    # Optional mirror token.
    # The token will be used as a bearer token in the Authorization header
    # Default: ''
    mirror-token: ''
```
<!-- end usage -->

**Basic:**

```yaml
steps:
- uses: actions/checkout@v6
- uses: actions/setup-node@v6
  with:
    node-version: 24
- run: npm ci
- run: npm test
```

The `node-version` input is optional. If not supplied, the node version from PATH will be used. However, it is recommended to always specify Node.js version and not rely on the system one.

The action will first check the local cache for a semver match. If unable to find a specific version in the cache, the action will attempt to download a version of Node.js. It will pull LTS versions from [node-versions releases](https://github.com/actions/node-versions/releases) and on miss or failure will fall back to the previous behavior of downloading directly from [node dist](https://nodejs.org/dist/).

For information regarding locally cached versions of Node.js on GitHub hosted runners, check out [GitHub Actions Runner Images](https://github.com/actions/runner-images).

### Supported version syntax

The `node-version` input supports the Semantic Versioning Specification, for more detailed examples please refer to [the semver package documentation](https://github.com/npm/node-semver).

Examples:

 - Major versions: `22`, `24`
 - More specific versions: `20.19`, `22.17.1` , `24.8.0`
 - NVM LTS syntax: `lts/iron`, `lts/jod`, `lts/*`, `lts/-n`

name: Build Binaries

on:
  push:
    tags:
      - 'v*'
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      tag:
        description: 'Tag to build (e.g., v0.12.0)'
        required: true

jobs:
  build:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    permissions:
      contents: write
    env:
      RELEASE_TAG: ${{ github.event.inputs.tag || github.ref_name }}
      SOURCE_REF: ${{ github.event.inputs.source_ref || github.event.inputs.tag || github.ref_name }}
    steps:
      - name: Checkout
        uses: actions/checkout@11bd71901bbe5b1630ceea73d27597364c9af683 # v4.2.2

        with:

      - name: Build binaries
        run: ./scripts/build-binaries.sh

        id: changelog

# Fork Changelog

Fork-specific changes maintained by valkyriweb. Upstream package changelogs stay reserved for upstream release notes and upstreamable changes.

## [Unreleased]

### Fixed

- **Background-job wakes survived two failure modes that left idle sessions parked forever** (`packages/coding-agent/src/core/tools/bash.ts`, `core/agent-session.ts`; entry covers `b1fcbc66`). (1) **Crash/signal-death of a `run_in_background` bash job was silently swallowed** — the exit handler only fired the terminal notification for a clean `"exited"` status, so a process killed by a signal (SIGSEGV, OOM SIGKILL, an external SIGTERM) landed as `"killed"` and never woke the agent. It now wakes on any terminal transition the agent did *not* initiate: deliberate stops (`bash_kill`/dispose/`killAll`) flip status off `"running"` *before* the exit fires and stay silent as before, but a signal death while still `"running"` now notifies (status `killed`, with `signal`). This silence is now race-safe on both edges: a deliberate `bash_kill` whose target already exited (`killProcessTree` throws `ESRCH`) still marks the job `killed` (and reports success) instead of leaving it `"running"` and tripping a spurious wake, and both background `error` handlers gained the same `wasRunning` gate so a `spawn`-error event on an already-stopped job stays silent too (regression test `test/bash-bg-kill-esrch.test.ts`). (2) **The idle-wake debounce timer dropped the wake if it fired mid-compaction** — the fire-once timer was already cleared, so a threshold/overflow compaction overlapping the 300 ms window stranded the notification in history with no retry; it now re-arms one debounce window later and fires once genuinely idle. Both paths covered by regression tests proven to fail on baseline and pass with the fix (`test/bash-background.test.ts`, `test/suite/agent-session-wake-on-idle.test.ts`). CC `<task-notification>` parity: a crashed/killed background job is a first-class terminal event, not a special silent path.

### Added

- **Extension event contexts can reload runtime resources directly** (`packages/coding-agent/src/core/extensions/{types,runner}.ts`, `core/agent-session.ts`, `modes/interactive/interactive-mode.ts`). `ctx.reload()` is now available on normal extension event handlers, not only slash-command handlers, so provider-family model-switch extensions can rebuild extension/package membership before the next provider request without queuing a slash command into the transcript. Regression: `packages/coding-agent/test/extensions-runner.test.ts` asserts `ExtensionContext.reload()` calls the bound runtime reload action.
- **`Tool.anthropicServerTool` sentinel (`packages/ai`): tool definitions opt into Anthropic server-tool blocks explicitly; name-based web_fetch/web_search interception dropped and `syncClaudeBridgeNativeTools` neutered** — client-side CC-parity web tools in my-pi are provider-agnostic; explicit opt-in beats name magic. Logged in `my-pi/docs/pi-fork-patch-inventory.md`; upstream PR candidate. (Entry added retroactively for `c87622dd7` — committed without its changelog line.)
- **Footer: first post-compaction turn's cold cache write rendered as expected, not drift.** The first assistant turn after a compaction rewrites the full prefix — a one-time expected cache write — but the footer alarm-colored it (red `cache 28%`). It now renders dim `cache N% ⟳compact` for that turn only; normal drift thresholds resume from turn 2. CC `notifyCompaction()` analog — the compaction session entry is the signal, no new event. (platform; cc-memory-parity-plan Phase 3)

- **Server-side advisor tool (`advisor_20260301`) for claude-bridge models** (`packages/ai` anthropic provider): typed server tool passes through un-prefixed and renders advisory output; pairs with the my-pi advisor extension (valkyriweb/my-pi#169).

### Changed

- **Synced upstream `earendil-works/pi-mono` 0.79.1 -> 0.79.3 (`6f29450e`, merge).** Took upstream releases v0.79.2/v0.79.3 plus the current adaptive-thinking model expectation fix, kept the fork's `@valkyriweb/*` package scope with all fork workspace package versions/internal deps at `0.79.3`, preserved Anthropic pause-turn/raw stop-reason behavior while adopting upstream refusal `stop_details`, and regenerated the root lockfile plus coding-agent shrinkwrap. Full `npm run check`, `npm run build` (including `test:build-gate` + sibling `my-pi` extension gate), and compiled `dist/pi --version` (`0.79.3`) passed.

- **Synced upstream `earendil-works/pi-mono` 0.79.1 (`0ab2aa86a` → `406a2214a`, merge).** One upstream commit: refined first-time-setup copy (now mentions `/privacy`). 10 conflicts resolved mechanically: 4× `package.json` kept `@valkyriweb/*` names exact-pinned; lock/shrinkwrap regenerated; `supports-xhigh.test.ts` kept the fork's capability-based suite (upstream's added Bedrock Fable 5 test duplicated an existing fork test); `startup-ui.ts`/`settings-manager.ts`/`first-time-setup.ts` kept fork import scope while taking upstream's refined setup copy. Full `npm run check` green.

- **Slimmed the Bash tool description to contract-only prose (~2KB/request saved).** The description repeated promptGuidelines coaching (background-mode etiquette, monitor_start, TUI-only use cases, native-tool detail) verbatim; that guidance already ships once via the system prompt. Kept: truncation limits, timeout, `run_in_background`, `tui_only`, and the native-file-tools pointer. One-time cache prefix re-warm on rollout. Refs valkyriweb/my-pi#170.

- **Synced upstream `earendil-works/pi-mono` 0.79.0 → 0.79.1 (`0ab2aa86a`, merge).** 19 upstream commits: Claude Fable 5 thinking-level support (anthropic-messages + bedrock-converse-stream, `off: null` + xhigh), opt-in analytics settings (`enableAnalytics`/`trackingId`), first-time-setup component, experimental-feature gating in startup UI. 10 conflicts resolved mechanically: 4× `package.json` kept `@valkyriweb/*` names exact-pinned at upstream's 0.79.1; `generate-models.ts` kept both the fork opus-4-8 xhigh branch and upstream's fable-5 branch; `supports-xhigh.test.ts` kept the fork's capability-based suite (issues #30/#33) and appended upstream's fable-5 pinned-id tests (+ `getModel` import restored in `anthropic-thinking-disable` / `bedrock-thinking-payload` tests); `startup-ui.ts`/`settings-manager.ts` kept fork import scope + upstream's new imports/fields; new upstream `first-time-setup.ts` rescoped to `@valkyriweb/pi-tui`; lockfile + shrinkwrap regenerated. Full `npm run check` green.

- **Synced upstream `earendil-works/pi-mono` 0.79.0 → `d041b5cc` (merge).** ~24 upstream commits (project-trust rework + approval-settings UI, experimental-feature guard, OAuth/help/CJK fixes, amazon-bedrock ARN region parsing, model-registry regen). Six conflicts resolved across the project-trust / cache-heartbeat / queued-recall seam, adversarially reviewed (6-agent workflow). **Notable fork divergence preserved:** upstream removed the `projectTrusted` parameter from `loadProjectContextFiles` and stopped passing it at the call site (project-local `AGENTS.md`/context files load unconditionally in upstream's model — trust gates only extensions/packages). The fork **keeps** its context-file trust gate as a prompt-injection defense: the fork's function body (with the `projectTrusted` guard + realpath dedup) is retained **and** `projectTrusted: this.settingsManager.isProjectTrusted()` was re-wired at the `reload()` call site (the merge had silently dropped it, neutering the gate — caught in review). Other resolutions: kept the fork's `agents`-command help block, `CacheHeartbeat*` settings, queued-recall hotkey text, richer extension `createContext` (now also carrying upstream's new `isProjectTrusted` field), and the `@valkyriweb/*` scope rename on the new upstream `startup-ui.ts`.
- **Bash `workdir` parameter (Codex `exec_command` parity) — closes the measured #1 cd-waste gap.** The core bash tool (`packages/coding-agent/src/core/tools/bash.ts`) gains an optional `workdir` (absolute, or relative to the session cwd) so a single call can run in another directory instead of `cd <dir> && …`. `execute()` resolves `effectiveCwd = workdir ? resolve(cwd, workdir) : cwd` and threads it through the only three cwd use-sites: the redundant-cd guard, the background spawn (`spawnBashBackground`, which validates existence → clear "Working directory does not exist" error), and the foreground spawn (`resolveSpawnContext` → `ops.exec`). Omitting `workdir` is byte-identical to prior behaviour; the redundant-cd guard now correctly keys off `effectiveCwd`. The existing `hasBash` system-prompt guideline (`system-prompt.ts`) was updated to point the model at `workdir` first (single source, no new duplicate bullet — the per-turn-billed tool description was intentionally left unchanged to avoid permanent token cost). **Motivation:** measured ~24 cd-bearing bash calls/session (48%) vs Codex ~0.25 (0.08%); Codex avoids cd via a first-class `workdir` used on 99% of calls — a tool-affordance gap, not a prompting one (core already shipped cd-avoidance guidance and the waste persisted). Generic platform primitive that cannot be exposed through the `prepareArguments` extension hook (no access to the spawn cwd), so it lives in core per the fork-patch policy; logged in `my-pi/docs/pi-fork-patch-inventory.md`. **Cache:** adds one optional schema property → the bash `tools[]` bytes change once (a single cold re-warm across sessions), then stable; no per-session variability. Regression: `test/bash-workdir.test.ts` (5 cases: absolute/relative/default cwd, non-existent-dir error, guard keys off effectiveCwd).
- **Render Anthropic provider-executed server tools (`web_search` / `web_fetch`) as TUI activity cards.** The Anthropic provider (`packages/ai`) now parses `server_tool_use` and `web_search_tool_result` / `web_fetch_tool_result` content blocks into display-only `server_tool_use` / `server_tool_result` stream events (new `ServerToolSource` type + two `AssistantMessageEvent` variants). They are intentionally **never** added to `AssistantMessage.content`, so the agent loop never executes them and they never round-trip to the API (cache- and replay-safe). The agent loop (`packages/agent`) forwards these through `message_update`; the interactive TUI (`packages/coding-agent`) renders them via a new `ServerToolActivityComponent` (query/URL + result sources), so these provider-side tools — which previously ran invisibly because they arrive as server-tool blocks rather than ordinary `tool_use` — now show up. Fork feature; logged here per the changelog-ownership split below.
- **Edit queued messages with the up arrow (interactive TUI).** When the agent is busy and you've queued a message, pressing ↑ in an empty editor recalls the most-recently-queued message into the editor for editing (recall priority: compaction-queued → follow-ups → steering). Recall lifts it out of the queue, so re-submitting replaces what was queued and clearing the editor (backspace to empty) drops it. If nothing is queued, ↑ falls through to footer nav / prompt history as before. Adds `Agent.removeLastSteeringMessage()` / `removeLastFollowUpMessage()` / `PendingMessageQueue.removeLast()` (`packages/agent`) and `AgentSession.popLastQueuedMessage()` (`packages/coding-agent`), wired through the existing `onPreInput` editor seam (no `custom-editor.ts` change). Recalled image attachments come back as text only, matching existing dequeue behaviour.

### Changed

- **`npm run build` (package `coding-agent`) now produces the compiled `dist/pi` binary; `build:ts` is the compile-only step.** Typing `npm run build` previously ran only `tsgo`, leaving the `bun`-compiled `dist/pi` (what the launcher execs) stale — source/test changes appeared to build but the running binary silently lagged, masking live behaviour. `build` is now the former `build:binary` (deps + `build:ts` + `bun build --compile` → `dist/pi` + copy-binary-assets); `build:ts` is the former compile-only step; `build:binary` stays as a back-compat alias to `build`. CI/publish/orchestration callers that only need the TS dist were repointed to `build:ts` (root `build`, `release.yml` npm publish, `agentic-review.yml` node-shim engine) so none start bun-compiling a 73 MB binary unexpectedly; `build-binaries.sh`/`ci.yml` use the root `build` (TS + gate) and compile per-platform separately, unaffected.

- **Slimmed the upstream-owned package changelogs (400KB → stubs) and flipped them to fork-owned `merge=ours`.** The package `CHANGELOG.md` files carried `earendil-works/pi-mono`'s full Keep-a-Changelog history and grew unbounded because `.gitattributes` `*CHANGELOG.md merge=union` made every sync *append* (never replace) — `coding-agent` reached 407KB. This both staled the files (the fork's real notes live here in `FORK-CHANGELOG.md`) and broke the release: `changesets/action` couldn't match the `## [x.y.z] - date` headings to the version, so it dumped the whole file as the GitHub Release body, exceeding the 125000-char cap (`422`). Archived each `packages/*/CHANGELOG.md` → `CHANGELOG.upstream.md` (frozen reference, full history preserved), reset `CHANGELOG.md` to a fork-owned stub pointing at `FORK-CHANGELOG.md` + the archive, and changed `.gitattributes`: `packages/*/CHANGELOG.md merge=ours` (fork keeps its stub across syncs — no re-bloat) with the `.upstream.md` archives staying `merge=union`. Changesets stays `changelog: false` (it never wrote these). This is the deliberate ownership change deferred from the release hotfix; the release-side bounded-body fix (`createGithubReleases:false` + `create-github-releases.mjs`) already keeps publishing safe and is unaffected. See `docs/adr/0002-slim-upstream-changelogs.md`.

### Fixed

- **Background bash jobs now wake the agent on completion (`#bash-bg-completion-wake`) — the documented notification was never wired for bash.** A `run_in_background:true` bash command ran, completed, updated the TUI footer via `notifyBashBgJobsChanged()`, and pushed **nothing** to the model. Only background *agent* runs had a wake path (`onBackgroundTerminal` → `AgentSession._emitAgentCompletion` → `sendCustomMessage`); the bash tool description still inherited Claude Code's promise ("you'll be notified when it finishes") and `core/tools/background-tasks.ts` even documented "Output is push-notified on completion", but the bash side of that wiring never existed. Net effect: a CC-trained model narrated "they'll wake me when done" and parked forever on a wake that never came. Fix mirrors the agent path: a `subscribeBashBgTerminal` listener registry in `core/tools/bash.ts` fires once on **natural** termination only (process exit / spawn error — explicit `bash_kill`, `killAll`, and session dispose deliberately do **not** fire, since the agent already knows it stopped them); `AgentSession.emitBashCompletion(job)` builds a `<task_notification>` custom message (task id, status, exit code, command, elapsed, output log path) and delivers it via `deliverAs: "followUp"` exactly like `_emitAgentCompletion`; the single **main interactive session** wires the subscription in `interactive-mode.ts` (the bg-bash store is process-global, so subscribing here rather than in every forked child session avoids duplicate notifications). The bash tool description + guideline were reworded to truthfully promise the wake and tell the model not to poll or re-run to "check" (one-time `tools[]` cache re-warm, then stable). Regression: `test/bash-background.test.ts` (natural-exit fires once with `status: exited`/`exit 0`; explicit kill fires zero times). Logged in `my-pi/docs/pi-fork-patch-inventory.md`.
- **Release publish no longer 422s on the upstream changelog size ("body is too long").** The `Release` workflow used `changesets/action`'s default `createGithubReleases: true`, which builds each package's GitHub Release body by matching a heading whose text equals the version (`## 0.31.0`). The fork's package `CHANGELOG.md` files are upstream-owned Keep-a-Changelog (`## [0.31.0] - 2026-01-02`, `coding-agent` is 400KB+ via `merge=union`), so the match always fails and the action falls back to dumping the **entire file** as the body — exceeding GitHub's 125000-char Release-body cap → `422` → the whole publish job reds (sometimes after publishing to the registry but before every Release is cut). Set `createGithubReleases: false` and added `.github/scripts/create-github-releases.mjs`, a post-publish step that cuts a Release per just-published package (from `steps.changesets.outputs.publishedPackages`) with a small, bounded body pointing at `FORK-CHANGELOG.md` — never the upstream changelog. The upstream-owned changelogs and `merge=union` are left untouched (slimming them is deferred to a separate ownership change with its own ADR). Idempotent (skips packages that already have a Release). Mirrors the same fix in the `my-pi` repo (#139).
- **`biome check` no longer breaks on stray local Pi workspaces.** `.pi/workspaces/` is gitignored globally but not in the repo `.gitignore`, and Biome's `vcs.useIgnoreFile` only reads the repo-local ignore — so a leftover workspace (e.g. `.pi/workspaces/upstream-tti/biome.json` from an upstream-sync session) was discovered as a nested root config and aborted `npm run check` repo-wide. Added `.pi/workspaces/` to the repo `.gitignore` so Biome skips it for everyone (matching the existing `.pi/workflows/` entry).
- **Extension loader resolves upstream package names (`@earendil-works/*`, `@mariozechner/*`).** The fork renamed its packages to `@valkyriweb/*`, but third-party extensions in the ecosystem still import the upstream scopes — `@earendil-works/*` (current upstream) and `@mariozechner/*` (legacy). Type-only imports erase at runtime, but extensions with **value** imports (e.g. pi-autoresearch pulling `truncateTail`/`formatSize`/`StringEnum`/`Text` as runtime values) failed to load with `Cannot find module "@mariozechner/pi-coding-agent"`. Added compatibility entries for both upstream scopes mapping onto the same fork modules, in **both** resolution paths: `getAliases()` (jiti, Node/dev mode) and `VIRTUAL_MODULES` (the compiled Bun binary that live `pi` actually runs — line 682 selects `virtualModules` over `alias` when `isBunBinary`). Covers `pi-coding-agent`, `pi-agent-core`, `pi-tui`, `pi-ai`, and `pi-ai/oauth`. Generic platform compatibility primitive (extension module resolution) that can't be expressed through hooks — restores the third-party extension ecosystem on the fork without each extension needing a `@valkyriweb/*` rewrite.
- **`setActiveToolsByName` cache-burst no-op guard (cache law #4).** Before rewriting `agent.state.tools` and rebuilding the system prompt, the method now early-returns when the freshly built `tools[]` is element-for-element **reference-identical** to the current state. An unconditional refresh on every `tools_changed`/`_refreshToolRegistry` event bursts the within-session `tools[]` (and system-prompt) cache prefix even when nothing actually changed. Reference-equality (not name-set equality) is the correct test: pi rebuilds the registry with fresh object refs whenever a definition changes (a tool gains `deferLoading`, an allowlist empties), so a genuine change yields different refs and the rebuild proceeds — only a true no-op early-returns (mirrors pi-ai's `convertedToolCache` WeakMap keyed by tool reference). Guard is skipped until the base prompt has been built once (`_baseSystemPromptOptions` is set only by `_rebuildSystemPrompt`), so the cold init `empty→empty` rebuild still runs. Same change adds the post-registration **deferral-override seam** (`setDeferredToolOverrides`/`_applyDeferredOverrides`): extensions can force already-registered tools to `deferLoading:true` so they ride `tools[]` as `defer_loading` stubs across every registry rebuild, with the same unchanged-set no-op guard (`sameStringSet`) so a redundant call doesn't burst the prefix. Also threads the live agent state into `createPromptCacheAffinityKey` on every model switch so the affinity key tracks the actual model rather than a stale cwd-only key.
- **Changelog guard: package-level test-only changes no longer wrongly require a CHANGELOG.** `requiredChangelog()` in `scripts/check-changelog-updated.mjs` returned the package `CHANGELOG.md` for any `packages/<pkg>/` path before consulting `isIgnored()` (which already covers test-only paths via `isTestOnly()`), so a change touching only `packages/<pkg>/test/**` failed the guard, contradicting the script's own "tests-only ... are ignored" message and the AGENTS changelog rules. Now `isIgnored(path)` is checked first (returns no requirement), then package/fork resolution. Verified with crafted diffs: a package test-only change passes, a package src change without its CHANGELOG still fails.

- **`fork-safety-check` CI: reordered `npm run build` so the four workspace packages build before `test:build-gate` runs.** The root `build` script ran `test:build-gate` first, but the gate's `test:e2e` step (`packages/coding-agent` `test/suite`) imports `@valkyriweb/pi-tui/dist/index.js` via `modes/interactive/theme/theme.ts`.
