That broke prompt-cache continuity: the moment a stripped tool_use appeared in parent's actual cached prefix, every subsequent block in the child's request diverged byte-for-byte from the parent's cache key, busting cache reuse for the entire leading section. New behavior mirrors Claude Code 2.1.x `buildForkedMessages` (`src/tools/AgentTool/forkSubagent.ts`): keep parent's `tool_use` blocks in place, and for any unresolved `tool_use` (denied or simply incomplete at fork time) synthesize a fixed-bytes placeholder `tool_result` with text `"Sibling agent task in progress."`. New helper `substitutePlaceholdersForUnresolvedToolCalls` is exported alongside `getFilteredForkMessages`. The placeholder text is identical across every fork child spawned from the same parent state, so **sibling forks share cache with each other**, not just with the parent — the critical property for wide parallel fan-out via `tasks[]`. Cache parity contract: any two `getFilteredForkMessages(parentSession)` calls return byte-identical arrays through every leading block, with the per-child user directive (built by `buildChildTaskPrompt`) as the only divergence point. Removed the now-dead `filterDeniedToolArtifacts` helper; left a comment marker so future maintainers see the historical rationale. Regression tests in `packages/coding-agent/test/agent-context-inheritance.test.ts`: "fork filtering keeps parent agent/subagent tool_uses for cache parity", "fork filtering substitutes placeholders for unresolved tool_uses, drops orphan results", and "sibling forks produce byte-identical message arrays" (JSON.stringify equality on two consecutive `getFilteredForkMessages` calls). Side note: orphan `tool_result`s (results whose `tool_use` doesn't exist in the message stream) are still dropped — those would confuse the provider API and don't appear in parent's cached prefix anyway.

- Added **B5 TUI slot extension hooks** to the `ExtensionAPI`: `pi.registerMainPane(id, factory)` / `showMainPane(id, payload?)` / `hideMainPane(id)` (push a component into `chatContainer`'s content stack); `pi.registerOverlay(id, factory)` / `showOverlay(id, payload?)` / `hideOverlay(id)` (durable overlay registration, distinct from one-shot `ui.custom()`); `pi.registerFooter(id, spec)` (contribute a focusable child into the existing footer's nav chain without owning the whole footer; reactive `visible()` predicate). Spatial/slot extension points (`register*`) deliberately distinct from temporal hooks (`on*` for `session_start`/`turn_end`/etc.). Runner exposes `getRegisteredMainPane(id)`, `getRegisteredOverlay(id)`, `getRegisteredFooters()`, plus `bindSlotUI()` for UI-capable modes (interactive) to back the imperative show/hide API; non-UI modes (RPC/print) keep the default no-op stubs so show/hide calls silently swallow. Implementation lands the hook surface; the interactive-mode mount-into-`chatContainer` wiring lives in the fork-only zoom consumer (issue 12 extracts that into `pi-agent-ui`). Design [`docs/plans/b5-tui-hooks-design-proposal-2026-05-21.md`](my-pi/docs/plans/b5-tui-hooks-design-proposal-2026-05-21.md) approved by Luke 2026-05-22; 14 unit tests in `extensions-runner-b5-hooks.test.ts` cover registration, show/hide delegation, first-registration-wins, reactive footer visibility, and no-registration baseline.
- Added `triggerTokens` to `compaction` settings — an absolute context-token threshold for auto-compaction. When the active model's context window is known, Pi derives `reserveTokens` as `contextWindow - triggerTokens`; otherwise falls back to the configured `reserveTokens`. Not yet upstream (FORK-CHANGELOG previously claimed PR #5 — that PR is unrelated; no upstream PR exists for this change as of 2026-05-21).
- Added `run_in_background`, `bash_output(bgId)`, and `bash_kill(bgId)` to the built-in `bash` tool, mirroring Claude Code's `BashOutput`/`KillShell` API. Background jobs spawn detached (POSIX), append stdout/stderr to `~/.pi/agent/bash-bg/<bgId>.log`, and the registry is reaped via `killAllBashBgJobs()` from `AgentSession.dispose()` so processes don't leak across `/clear`, fork, switchSession, reload, or final shutdown. Bounded log slices for `bash_output`, idempotent `bash_kill`, and a teardown test that confirms registry cleanup.
- Added `settings.subagents` — default model and thinking config for native child agents. Supports a global `defaults` block and a `providers[<parent.provider>]` map. Precedence: explicit task option > agent frontmatter > `subagents.providers[parent.provider]` > `subagents.defaults` > parent inheritance. Wired end-to-end through `runChild` and `resumeSingleBackgroundRun` via a new `resolveAgentDefaults()` helper; covered by one unit test per precedence layer plus an integration test that reads through `SettingsManager.getSubagentSettings()`.
- **Phase 2b** — Real-session rendering in the TUI zoom view. When zooming into a running background agent, the view now subscribes to the child `AgentSession`'s live event stream and renders its transcript using `AssistantMessageComponent` and `ToolExecutionComponent` — identical widgets to the parent session. Streaming assistant text **mutates in place** via `updateContent()`, so no duplicate-prefix lines appear as tokens stream in. Tool calls render with expandable output and edit-diff widgets. Implemented via: a new `core/agents/live-sessions.ts` module-level registry (`registerLiveSession`/`unregisterLiveSession`/`getLiveSession`); `executor.ts` registers the child session before driving the prompt loop and deregisters in the `finally` block; `ZoomedSessionTranscript` component in `components/zoomed-session-transcript.ts` subscribes to the session on construction and disposes cleanly; `ZoomedTaskComponent` uses the transcript when a live session is available and falls back to the Phase 1 `TaskMessageEvent` tail for terminal/replay tasks. Parent session settings (cwd, `hideThinkingBlock`, markdown theme, image options) are passed via `ZoomedSessionConfig`. Inject + auto-pop behaviour is unchanged. New test: `zoomed-session-transcript.test.ts` (5 cases: in-place text mutation, tool widget lifecycle, dispose/unsubscribe, registry round-trip, undefined for missing session).
- **Phase 2a** — Footer pill navigation for the TUI zoom view. Pressing `up` on an empty editor with ≥1 running background agent enters footer-nav mode: each running agent is shown as a pill in the footer status line, with the selected pill highlighted in accent bold. `up`/`down` cycle through running agents (wrap-around), `enter` zooms into the selected agent, `escape` cancels without zooming. Keybindings registered as `app.agents.footer.focusPrev` (default `up`), `app.agents.footer.focusNext` (default `down`), `app.agents.footer.zoom` (default `enter`) in `DEFAULT_APP_KEYBINDINGS`. Fall-through to normal editor behaviour when editor is non-empty or no running tasks exist. Implemented via a new `onPreInput` hook on `CustomEditor` that runs before extension shortcuts. Footer selection clears automatically on text input and on escape. The `alt+z` power-user shortcut (`app.agents.zoom.enter`) is preserved. Works in terminals without option-as-alt (e.g. Rusty Warp) because defaults use plain arrow keys. New test: `interactive-mode-footer-nav.test.ts` (8 cases covering focus-prev/next, wrap-around, clear-on-text, propagation to footer component, zoom on enter, no-op with no running tasks).
- Added a TUI zoom-into-running-agent view. Pressing `app.agents.zoom.enter` (default `alt+z`) swaps the main chat pane for a `ZoomedTaskComponent` that renders the live tail of `TaskMessageEvent`s for the most recent running background agent. While zoomed, Enter routes to `LocalAgentTask.injectMessage(taskId, text)` instead of the parent session and emits an immediate `user_injected` event so the operator sees confirmation before the child picks the message up at its next turn. `app.agents.zoom.cycleNext`/`cyclePrev` (default `alt+l`/`alt+h`) walk the shared `getRunningTasksSorted()` order — the same canonical sort used by the footer pill, mirroring Claude Code's `getRunningTeammatesSorted` invariant. `app.agents.zoom.requestShutdown` (default `alt+i`) and `app.agents.zoom.kill` (default `alt+k`) call `LocalAgentTask.requestShutdown` / `kill`. When the zoomed task reaches a terminal status (`completed | failed | cancelled | killed`) the view auto-pops after `STOPPED_DISPLAY_MS` (3s) via a `subscribeAgentRecentRuns` listener + `isTerminalTaskStatus` check. New `core/tasks/sort.ts` exposes `getRunningTasksSorted()` and `cycleRunningTask()`. All keybindings live in `DEFAULT_APP_KEYBINDINGS` (no hardcoded `matchesKey` literals). Regression coverage: `tasks-sort.test.ts` (helper) and `interactive-mode-zoom.test.ts` (component + integration) — plus a tmux smoke script at `packages/coding-agent/test/tmux/zoom-smoke.sh` for end-to-end TTY verification (gated outside vitest because it needs a real provider).
- Added push-based background-agent completion notifications. When a background `agent` run (or `ctx.forkAgent`) reaches a terminal status (`completed | failed | cancelled | interrupted`), the parent session is sent an `agent_completion` custom message carrying `runId`, `status`, `summary`, `result` preview, `output_path`s, `session_path`s, `duration_ms`, `total_tokens`, and `tool_calls`. Mirrors Claude Code's `<task_notification>` shape. The notification fires exactly once per run (atomic dedup via a per-run `notified` flag inside `agents/status.ts`) and is delivered as a `followUp`, so `message_start` fires when the loop picks it up — which is exactly the wake signal pi-goal's `goal_wait` listens for. The `agent` tool's prompt guidelines now explicitly say "do not poll with action=status/detail while waiting”, matching Claude Code's anti-polling rule. New extension hook point: `AgentToolOptions.onBackgroundTerminal(notification)` and `AgentExecutorOptions.onBackgroundTerminal`, wired into the session's `sendCustomMessage` path.
- Added `ctx.forkAgent(opts)` to `ExtensionContext`: spawns a cache-preserving background child agent in `context: "fork"` mode, inheriting the parent's frozen turn-start system prompt 1:1 (byte-identical system + tools prefix for cache hits). Returns `{ handle, sessionId }` where `handle.wait()` resolves with the run's terminal `AgentToolDetails`, `handle.abort()` cancels within ~1s, and `handle.status` snapshots the current `AgentToolStatus`. Caller signal is chained via `cancelAgentRecentRun(runId)`.
- Added `ctx.transcript.append(entry)` to `ExtensionContext` with `TranscriptEntry = { kind: "memory_saved"; verb: "Saved" | "Improved"; paths: string[] }`. Routes through `sendCustomMessage` with `customType: "memory_saved"` so the entry serializes through every mode (interactive renders inline, print/RPC see it in the event stream).
- Added a built-in `memory_saved` message renderer in the interactive TUI (`MemorySavedMessageComponent`). Extension-registered renderers still win; the built-in is a fallback so extensions can append memory entries without shipping their own renderer.
- Added a `"fast"` model alias for the built-in `agent` tool, resolving to the parent provider's mapped cheap variant (Anthropic→Haiku, OpenAI→gpt-5.4-mini, Google→Flash Lite, claude-bridge→Haiku, etc.) via `fastModelPerProvider` in `model-resolver.ts`. Falls back to the parent model when the provider has no mapping. The built-in `explore` agent now defaults to `model: "fast"` so codebase research no longer burns the parent's expensive model.
- Added native background lifecycle control for the built-in `agent` tool, including background launch, footer visibility, selectable `/agents runs` controls, `/agents-status` visibility, interrupt/cancel, and single-run resume.
- Added `pi-agent-tool/eval-design-prompt.md` to design a token-efficient A/B eval comparing native Pi agents with `pi-subagents`.
- Added a native built-in `agent` tool with single, parallel, and chain modes, built-in child agent definitions, user/project Markdown discovery, context modes, `/agents`, and migration docs for the legacy `subagent` extension example.
- Added native-search backend selection for the built-in `grep` and `find` tools, preferring controlled/system `ugrep` and `bfs` before falling back to managed/system `rg` and `fd`.
- Documented Claude Code native search-tool findings and the planned `ugrep`/`bfs` backend direction for Pi's built-in `grep` and `find` tools.

### Changed

- Compact skill listings in the system prompt by rendering each skill as a single XML element and capping prompt descriptions, reducing loaded skill prompt text while preserving names and load paths.
- Tightened the built-in `explore` agent prompt to mirror Claude Code's read-only search specialist: explicit READ-ONLY prohibitions, parallel-tool guidance, caller-specified thoroughness levels (`quick` / `medium` / `very thorough`).
- Removed the built-in `scout` agent; it overlapped `explore`. `explore` is now the single read-only research agent.
- Updated the `agent` tool's prompt guidelines to route codebase research and file/symbol lookups to `explore` instead of `general`, and to prefer `plan` before delegating implementation to `worker`.
- Deferred the built-in `statusline-setup` agent until Pi's statusline target is defined.

### Fixed

- Made the built-in TUI footer context count use an extension-owned cached snapshot that includes the effective system prompt, active provider tool schemas, and transcript/provider usage. Provider tool schemas are top-level request `tools`, not system-prompt text, but still count against the context window; deferred tool index text counts only as prompt text until the full tool schema is active.
- Resolved Anthropic `stop_reason: "pause_turn"` **in-stream** inside `streamAnthropic` instead of mapping it to a terminal `"stop"` (`packages/ai/src/providers/anthropic.ts`). When a long-running server-side tool (`web_search` / `web_fetch` / `code_execution`) needs another turn to finish, Anthropic returns a partial assistant message and the client must echo it back unmodified to resume. The previous mapping let the partial turn reach the agent loop, which persisted it to the session JSONL. On the next user prompt or auto-compaction the partial turn replayed as the latest assistant message and any byte-level drift in a thinking signature triggered a hard 400 (`messages.N.content.M: \"thinking\" or \"redacted_thinking\" blocks in the latest assistant message cannot be modified`) that then poisoned every subsequent request, including compaction. Fix: capture the raw stop reason in `message_delta`, and while it's `pause_turn` (capped at 16 resumes) append the partial assistant message to `context.messages` and re-issue `client.messages.create` with the same `options.onPayload` hook and `requestOptions`. Signed thinking blocks round-trip byte-for-byte through the existing `transformMessages` + assistant-block builder path (`packages/ai/src/providers/anthropic.ts:~1163`), so the resumed request passes Anthropic's signature validation. The `mapStopReason("pause_turn")` arm stays as a defensive fallback (`"stop"`) for any caller wiring `mapStopReason` directly. Regression coverage: `packages/ai/test/anthropic-pause-turn-resume.test.ts` (single-resume happy path with thinking-signature preservation in the continuation payload; multi-resume loop walking three `pause_turn` responses before terminating; resume-limit cap surfacing an `"error"` stop reason with a clear message). (#thinking-roundtrip)
- Documented the **OpenClaw + pi-harness model-namespace ambiguity trap** in [`docs/openclaw-pi-harness-debug.md`](docs/openclaw-pi-harness-debug.md). When OpenClaw registers a custom agentRuntime against an invented prefix (`pi-fork/claude-sonnet-4-6`) instead of the real provider namespace (`claude-bridge/claude-sonnet-4-6`), `session-binding.ts` strips its own provider before spawning pi, leaving pi to resolve a bare `--model claude-sonnet-4-6` against an ambiguous registry (built-in `anthropic/...` vs custom `claude-bridge/...`). Pi defaults to the built-in `anthropic` entry, whose `baseUrl` is hardcoded to `https://api.anthropic.com` in `packages/ai/src/providers/anthropic.ts` (overrides `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL` env), and traffic skips the local OAuth bridge entirely — surfacing as a misleading `"You're out of extra usage"` 400 even when the Max plan is healthy. Doc captures the canonical fix (register the runtime against the underlying provider namespace), a triage runbook, and the bridge `/status` counter as ground-truth diagnostic for "did pi actually go through the bridge?". Reference fix: bermont-kube PR #60.
- Fixed zoomed background-agent pane input semantics. Extension main panes can now handle `Escape` before core falls back to hiding the pane; `pi-agent-ui` uses this so `Esc` interrupts the zoomed agent while `alt+z` or `/exit-zoom` exits zoom. Text entered while zoomed now queues into the live child `AgentSession` via `steer()` for running background agents, falling back to resume-with-prompt only for already-interrupted resumable runs. The zoom UI also shows explicit queued/error status for submitted input. Known limitation: zoom input queues agent messages; it does not write stdin into an active bash tool process.
- Improved interactive responsiveness under frequent render/status updates by scheduling TUI renders with `setImmediate` instead of `process.nextTick`, and caching footer cumulative usage totals between session-entry changes.
- Included the built-in `grep`, `find`, `ls`, and `agent` tools in the default active tool set so the system prompt exposes them when no explicit tool allowlist is configured.
- Added bounded default timeouts to the built-in `grep` and `find` tools with structured timeout results, partial output when available, AbortSignal preservation, and explicit `timeout` overrides up to 300 seconds.
- Fixed runtime active-tool changes made during tool execution so the next provider request in the same agent run receives the refreshed tool schema. This makes deferred-tool activators such as `tool_search` able to expose newly activated tools immediately, and deduplicates repeated active tool names.

### Removed

- Removed the fork-retained `packages/web-ui` workspace after upstream deleted it and local audit confirmed zero live consumers. Also removed the stale web-ui references from `tsconfig.json` and the pre-commit browser-smoke trigger.

## 2026-05-02

- Locally aliased the installed `pi-subagents` manager command from `/agents` to `/subagents` for A/B testing against native `/agents`; this lives under `~/.pi/agent/git/github.com/nicobailon/pi-subagents` and may be overwritten by `pi update`.
- Merged upstream `v0.72.0` into the fork.

*** Begin Patch
*** Update File: /Users/luke/Projects/personal/pi-mono-fork-update-0793/FORK-CHANGELOG.md
@@
 ## [Unreleased]
 
+### Changed
+
+- Versioned the fork packages as `0.79.4`, carrying the upstream `0.79.3` sync plus the extension event-context `ctx.reload()` patch into the publishable package set.
+
 ### Fixed
 
 - **Background-job wakes survived two failure modes that left idle sessions parked forever** (`packages/coding-agent/src/core/tools/bash.ts`, `core/agent-session.ts`; entry covers `b1fcbc66`). (1) **Crash/signal-death of a `run_in_background` bash job was silently swallowed** — the exit handler only fired the terminal notification for a clean `"exited"` status, so a process killed by a signal (SIGSEGV, OOM SIGKILL, an external SIGTERM) landed as `"killed"` and never woke the agent. It now wakes on any terminal transition the agent did *not* initiate: deliberate stops (`bash_kill`/dispose/`killAll`) flip status off `"running"` *before* the exit fires and stay silent as before, but a signal death while still `"running"` now notifies (status `killed`, with `signal`). This silence is now race-safe on both edges: a deliberate `bash_kill` whose target already exited (`killProcessTree` throws `ESRCH`) still marks the job `killed` (and reports success) instead of leaving it `"running"` and tripping a spurious wake, and both background `error` handlers gained the same `wasRunning` gate so a `spawn`-error event on an already-stopped job stays silent too (regression test `test/bash-bg-kill-esrch.test.ts`). (2) **The idle-wake debounce timer dropped the wake if it fired mid-compaction** — the fire-once timer was already cleared, so a threshold/overflow compaction overlapping the 300 ms window stranded the notification in history with no retry; it now re-arms one debounce window later and fires once genuinely idle. Both paths covered by regression tests proven to fail on baseline and pass with the fix (`test/bash-background.test.ts`, `test/suite/agent-session-wake-on-idle.test.ts`). CC `<task-notification>` parity: a crashed/killed background job is a first-class terminal event, not a special silent path.
*** End Patch

name: Release

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]

concurrency:
  group: release-${{ github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: false

permissions:

  pull-requests: write

jobs:
  release:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    env:
      ANTHROPIC_API_KEY: ""
      ANTHROPIC_OAUTH_TOKEN: ""
      OPENAI_API_KEY: ""
      GEMINI_API_KEY: ""
      GROQ_API_KEY: ""

      XAI_API_KEY: ""
      OPENROUTER_API_KEY: ""
      ZAI_API_KEY: ""

      MINIMAX_API_KEY: ""

      KIMI_API_KEY: ""
      AI_GATEWAY_API_KEY: ""
      OPENCODE_API_KEY: ""
      COPILOT_GITHUB_TOKEN: ""
      HF_TOKEN: ""
      GOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDENTIALS: ""
      GOOGLE_CLOUD_PROJECT: ""
      GCLOUD_PROJECT: ""
      GOOGLE_CLOUD_LOCATION: ""
      AWS_PROFILE: ""
      AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID: ""
      AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY: ""
      AWS_SESSION_TOKEN: ""
      AWS_REGION: ""
      AWS_DEFAULT_REGION: ""
      AWS_BEARER_TOKEN_BEDROCK: ""
      AWS_CONTAINER_CREDENTIALS_RELATIVE_URI: ""
      AWS_CONTAINER_CREDENTIALS_FULL_URI: ""
      AWS_WEB_IDENTITY_TOKEN_FILE: ""
      AZURE_OPENAI_API_KEY: ""
      AZURE_OPENAI_BASE_URL: ""
      AZURE_OPENAI_RESOURCE_NAME: ""
      PI_NO_LOCAL_LLM: "1"
    steps:
      - name: Checkout pi-mono fork
        uses: actions/checkout@v6
        with:
          path: pi-mono-fork
          fetch-depth: 0

      - name: Setup Node.js
        uses: actions/setup-node@v6
        with:
          node-version: '24'
          registry-url: 'https://npm.pkg.github.com'
          cache: npm
          cache-dependency-path: pi-mono-fork/package-lock.json

      - name: Install system dependencies
        run: sudo apt-get update && sudo apt-get install -y libcairo2-dev libpango1.0-dev libjpeg-dev libgif-dev librsvg2-dev fd-find ripgrep && sudo ln -s "$(which fdfind)" /usr/local/bin/fd

      - name: Install pi-mono dependencies
        working-directory: pi-mono-fork
        run: npm ci --ignore-scripts

      - name: Build packages
        working-directory: pi-mono-fork
        run: npm --prefix packages/tui run build && npm --prefix packages/ai run build && npm --prefix packages/agent run build && npm --prefix packages/coding-agent run build:ts

      - name: Release gate
        working-directory: pi-mono-fork
        run: npm run test:system-prompt && npm run test:cache-stability && npm run test:e2e

      - name: Fork canonical check
        working-directory: pi-mono-fork
        run: npm run check

      - name: Version or publish packages
        id: changesets
        uses: changesets/action@v1
        with:
          cwd: pi-mono-fork
          version: npm run version-packages
          publish: npm run publish:changesets
          commit: "chore(release): version fork packages"
          title: "chore(release): version fork packages"
          # We cut GitHub Releases ourselves (next step) with a bounded body.
          # The package CHANGELOG.md files are upstream-owned Keep-a-Changelog
          # (`## [x.y.z] - date`, 400KB+); the action can't match those headings
          # to the version, so it dumps the whole file as the Release body and
          # 422s past GitHub's 125000-char cap. See create-github-releases.mjs.
          createGithubReleases: false
        env:
          GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
          NODE_AUTH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}

      # Cut a GitHub Release per just-published package, with a small body that
      # points at FORK-CHANGELOG.md (never the 400KB upstream changelog), so a
      # Release is always created and publish never reds on changelog size.
      - name: Create GitHub Releases (bounded body)
        if: steps.changesets.outputs.published == 'true'
        working-directory: pi-mono-fork
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
        run: node .github/scripts/create-github-releases.mjs '${{ steps.changesets.outputs.publishedPackages }}'

## Code Quality

## Execution Policy
- Clear + reversible → act. Irreversible/destructive/private/external (send/post/delete/deploy) → ask first.
- One non-retrievable decision blocking safe progress → one concise question, not three.
- Newest user instruction wins conflicts.

## Tool Discipline
- Tool evidence over recall for action, state, or mutable facts; concrete path from user → `Read` it before asking.
- Smallest native parser: `jq` for JSON; `Read` for files; `Grep` for known text.
- Expensive/remote commands: run once, save to `/tmp`, inspect the file.
- Verify before deciding: classify from a concrete artifact (log line, test output, file:line). Test: *what evidence would change my mind?*
- 3-strike rule: same tool + same input 3× → stop; write what's known, what's unknown, and a different action.

## Agent & Tool Routing
- Read-only multi-file investigation → exploration agent. Implementation/mixed → general-purpose. Diff review → reviewer. Design-before-code → plan. Known file/symbol/error, ≤3 files → direct tools, no agent.
- Model floors: scouting → fast/low; mechanical edits → medium; planning/API design/migrations and adversarial review/architecture/security → frontier/high. Never fast/mini models for review, security, architecture, or completion audits for large tasks.
- GitHub URLs → prefer `gh`. WebSearch for past-cutoff/current/version-specific info; include the year. Cheap-and-narrow beats expensive-and-fuzzy.

## Skill Auto-load
Load the matching skill **before** the first tool call in that domain — auto-trigger isn't reliable. Don't claim a skill was used unless actually loaded. Skill wrappers beat raw runbook commands.

## Instruction & Skill Maintenance
- Budgets: skill `description` ≤250 chars = capability + "use when" triggers; SKILL.md body ≤~120 lines — rules/workflow inline, lookup tables & runbooks → `references/` with read-when pointers. Parents stay thin routers; demote children via `skillOverrides` in `~/.claude/settings.json`.

- Deploy skills: `python3 scripts/skills link --apply` (symlinks → Claude/Codex/Pi); dry-run first.

## Hygiene & Completion
- Stale docs/skills/contradictions spotted while working: fix small things in place; surface non-trivial/cross-cutting for approval; ask when intent unclear. Don't ignore rot.
- Todo incomplete until every requested item handled or marked **[blocked]**: *"items 1–3 done; 4 [blocked]: need <X>"*. Before "done": claims grounded + smallest meaningful gate run (test/typecheck/lint/build/screenshot/diff) — or say why none could.

## Z/L Continuum — Code Review Tiers
Classify every change at top of reply; ambiguous → classify up; user override wins.

| Tier | Scope | Handoff |
|---|---|---|
| **critical** | Core behavior of what's shipping now | Stop per diff, wait for approval; one critical → one cycle |
| **important** | Adjacent features, cross-cutting refactors, non-obvious intent | Batch diffs, summarize, wait for "go" |
| **routine** | Tests, fixtures, docs, lint/format, codegen, styling | Proceed; report at end |

## Communication
- Correctness over voice; style never trumps answer/format/safety. Lead with outcome; cite artifacts (paths, commands, errors). One-sentence narration before meaningful tool use, then the call in the same turn.
- Blocked on Luke for attention-sensitive input (auth, 1Password, npm/release gates, approvals, blockers) → `sag-luke --volume 0.65 "<short specific ask>"` + same request in chat. Rare and specific; never routine status.

## Parallel & Long Sessions
- Independent tasks → parallel; dependent → sequential. High-volume output → agent or background; multi-agent comms via temp files.
- Long sessions: exploration agents first for >5-file refactors; after architecture-heavy slices report done/yet-to-do, deviations, roadblocks; cross-session threads → `/tmp` handoff.

# /go

Announce at start: **"Using /go. Orchestrating verify → code-review polish → review gate → PR → CI-watch as clean-context subagents."**

You are the **orchestrator**. Phases run as sequential subagents except the review gate, which may fan out into parallel reviewers for non-trivial changes. File-based handoffs live in `./.go-output/`. The arc mirrors a manual ship cycle — clean up the diff, verify it works (surfacing regressions the request didn't ask about), get an independent review, open the PR, then watch CI and fix failures as they land — so the human can hand off the whole loop, not just the build.

## References

| Phase | Handoff template |
|---|---|
| 1 Verify | `references/phase-1-verify.md` |
| 2 Code Review | `references/phase-2-code-review.md` |
| 3 Review gate | `references/phase-3-code-craft.md`; non-trivial fan-out also uses `references/phase-3-security.md` and `references/phase-3-test-engineer.md`; UI changes also use `references/phase-3-design.md` |
| 4 PR | `references/phase-4-pr.md` |
| 5 CI watch | `references/phase-5-ci-watch.md` |

Each handoff is self-contained: the subagent gets the file's contents (with `{{CWD}}` interpolated), reads the artifacts from prior phases, and returns a single-line STATUS.

## File workspace

```
.go-output/
  context.md      # Phase 0 writes — scope, classification, commands
  verify.md       # Phase 1 writes
  slop-scan.md    # Phase 1 writes when slop-scan is available (advisory)
  verify-*.png    # Phase 1 writes (screenshots)
  code-review.md  # Phase 2 writes
  code-craft.md   # Phase 3 writes (## Fixed + ## Follow-ups)
  security.md     # Phase 3 fan-out writes when security review runs
  test-review.md  # Phase 3 fan-out writes when test review runs
  design.md       # Phase 3 fan-out writes when the diff touched UI
  review-gate.md  # Phase 3 synthesis writes
  pr.md           # Phase 4 writes (PR URL + commits)
  ci-watch.md     # Phase 5 writes (CI result + any autofix commits)
```

Create the directory in Phase 0 and add `.go-output/` to `.gitignore` if absent — these are ephemeral.

## Phase 0 — Orchestrator setup

1. Capture scope:
   ```bash
   git status --porcelain
   git diff --stat
   # If tree is clean and commits exist on a branch:
   base=$(git merge-base HEAD origin/main 2>/dev/null || git merge-base HEAD main)
   git log --oneline "$base"..HEAD
   git diff --stat "$base"..HEAD
   ```
2. **Detect unrelated changes.** Compare the modified files against the user's stated work. Any file that doesn't fit the intent (e.g. `scripts/debug.py` when the user is shipping `feat/csv-export`) is unrelated. If unrelated changes exist, halt before writing `context.md` and surface three options to the user: commit them on the current branch, stash them, or move them to a separate branch. Do not dispatch phases until resolved. Phases must never silently sweep unrelated work into the PR.
3. Classify the change as one or more of: `backend-cli`, `web-ui`, `desktop-native`, `refactor`.
   - **Determine `UI-touched`** — the single relevance gate for the Core Web Vitals trace (Phase 1) and the design review (Phase 3). Set `yes` only if the diff changes a rendered UI surface: components/templates/markup (`.tsx/.jsx/.vue/.svelte/.astro/.html/.blade.php`), styles (`.css/.scss/.less`, Tailwind classes), or design tokens. Pure logic, API, config, test, build, or docs changes are `no` — even when the app has a UI. When `no`, Phase 1 skips the CWV trace and Phase 3 skips the design reviewer; never spin up browser/perf tooling for a change that can't move a pixel.
4. Derive project commands from `AGENTS.md` / `README` / `package.json` scripts / nearest config:
   - `TEST_CMD`, `LINT_CMD` (or `none`), `TYPECHECK_CMD` (or `none`), dev-server command if web-ui or backend-cli.
   - `SLOP_SCAN_CMD`: use `npm run review:slop` when present, otherwise `npx slop-scan scan . --lint` for JS/TS repos with `slop-scan` available, otherwise `none`.
5. Scan the user's prompt for context the phases should preserve: flaky-test warnings, known-broken tests on main, infra caveats, reviewer preferences. These go in the `Notes` field of `context.md`.
6. `mkdir -p .go-output` and write `.go-output/context.md`:

   ```markdown
   # /go context
   - Branch: <branch>
   - Base: <base-sha>
   - Classification: <kinds>
   - UI-touched: <yes|no>   # gates CWV trace (Phase 1) + design review (Phase 3)
   - Changed files:
     <list>
   - Test cmd: <cmd>
   - Lint cmd: <cmd-or-none>
   - Typecheck cmd: <cmd-or-none>
   - Slop-scan cmd: <cmd-or-none>  # advisory heuristic, not a standalone blocker
   - Dev-server cmd: <cmd-or-na>
   - Summary: <one-line intent suitable for branch slug + PR title>
   - Notes: <anything unusual>
   ```

7. Print: `/go context written: <N> files, classified <kinds>, dispatching verify subagent.`

## Phases 1–4 — Dispatch

For phases 1, 2, 4, and 5, dispatch a subagent with:
- **Prompt** = contents of `references/phase-N-<name>.md` with `{{CWD}}` replaced by the absolute working directory.
- **Clean context** — do not carry parent conversation into the subagent.
- **Synchronous** — wait for the subagent to return before dispatching the next phase.

Harness mapping:
- **Claude Code** — `Agent` tool with `subagent_type: "general-purpose"`.
- **Pi** — Pi's agent SDK with a fresh context.
- **Codex** — `SendMessage` to a spawned subagent, or Codex's native spawn mechanism.

After each return, read the phase's artifact file and the STATUS line. Apply the early-stop rules below.

### Phase 3 — Review gate with optional fan-out

Before Phase 3, classify whether this is **trivial**. Skip fan-out only if all are true:

- touches 2 files or fewer;
- diff is under 50 changed lines;
- does not touch auth, payments, data access, config, secrets, network boundaries, migrations, CI, deployment, or permissioning;
- Phase 1 found no verification gaps.

If trivial, run only `references/phase-3-code-craft.md` as the code-craft reviewer.

If non-trivial, dispatch these clean-context reviewers in parallel from the orchestrator:

| Reviewer | Prompt |
|---|---|
| Code craft | `references/phase-3-code-craft.md` |
| Security | `references/phase-3-security.md` |
| Test engineer | `references/phase-3-test-engineer.md` |

#### Design review step (only when `UI-touched: yes`)

This is a first-class step of the review gate, not an optional extra. The rule is simple: **if `context.md` has `UI-touched: yes`, the design review runs; if `no`, it is skipped entirely.** It is gated on *touching UI*, not on diff size — a change small enough to be "trivial" in code terms (the video's like-button case) can still ship a contrast or layout-shift defect.

When `UI-touched: yes`, dispatch `references/phase-3-design.md` in parallel with the code reviewers above (it runs even when the code change is otherwise trivial). It consumes Phase 1's screenshots + Core Web Vitals and composes the `frontend` skill's `web-design-guidelines` and `taste-skill-anti-slop` references. A `DESIGN-NEEDS-WORK` verdict with unresolved blockers makes the gate `NO-GO`.

When `UI-touched: no`, do not dispatch it and do not load any browser/perf tooling — record `Design review: n/a (no UI surface)` in the synthesis.

Then synthesize their artifacts into `./.go-output/review-gate.md` with:

```markdown
## Decision
GO | NO-GO

## Required fixes before PR
<blockers with source artifact + file:line/evidence>

## Follow-ups
<non-blocking follow-ups>

## Rollback plan
<how to back out safely if this ships badly>
```

If any reviewer reports a blocker, stop before Phase 4 unless the fix is in-scope, applied, and the relevant tests are rerun green.

### Phase 5 — Watch CI and autofix

After Phase 4 opens a PR on GitHub, dispatch `references/phase-5-ci-watch.md` to watch CI and drive the PR to green. This phase composes the `autofix-pr` skill: it watches `gh pr checks --watch`, classifies each failure, fixes in-scope ones locally, gates, and pushes — looping until green or blocked.

Skip Phase 5 only when:

- Phase 4 returned `PUSHED-NO-PR` (no GitHub PR to watch), or
- the repo has no CI checks (`gh pr checks` reports an empty set after the first poll), or
- the user asked for the PR to stay a draft / explicitly opted out of CI babysitting in their prompt (record in `context.md` Notes).

Phase 5 **never merges**. It stops at green and leaves the merge decision to the human. Unrelated/flaky failures are reported, not force-fixed (see the reference for the prefer-merge-main-over-bloat rule).

## Early-stop rules

- Phase 1 `BLOCKED` → stop. Surface `verify.md` to the user. Do not code-review or PR broken code.
- Phase 2 `BROKE-AND-REVERTED` → continue. The revert restored the green state from Phase 1.
- Phase 3 `NO-GO` or unresolved blocker → stop. Surface `review-gate.md` and the contributing reviewer artifacts.
- Phase 3 `REVIEW-FIXED` with failing tests → the subagent should have reverted; if it didn't, stop before Phase 4 and surface.
- Phase 4 `BLOCKED` → surface the reason (common causes: no `gh` auth, branch protection, dirty tree). Leave retry to the human. Do not run Phase 5 without an open PR.
- Phase 4 `PUSHED-NO-PR` → skip Phase 5 (nothing to watch); surface the remote + branch.
- Phase 5 `CI-RED` after its autofix attempts are exhausted → stop. Surface `ci-watch.md` with the remaining failing checks and their log evidence. Never merge a red PR; never `--no-verify` or force-skip a check to make it look green.

## Orchestrator finish

Print:

```
/go complete.
- Verify: <status>
- Code Review: <status>
- Review gate: <status>
- Design review: <status | n/a (no UI surface)>
- PR: <url>
- CI watch: <status> (green | red — <n> checks | skipped — <reason>)
```

Leave `.go-output/` on disk. The user can delete it when the PR merges.

name: Release

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]

concurrency:
  group: release-${{ github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: false

permissions:

jobs:
  release:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    env:
      ANTHROPIC_API_KEY: ""
      ANTHROPIC_OAUTH_TOKEN: ""
      OPENAI_API_KEY: ""
      GEMINI_API_KEY: ""
      GROQ_API_KEY: ""
      CEREBRAS_API_KEY: ""
      XAI_API_KEY: ""
      OPENROUTER_API_KEY: ""
      ZAI_API_KEY: ""
      MISTRAL_API_KEY: ""
      MINIMAX_API_KEY: ""
      MINIMAX_CN_API_KEY: ""
      KIMI_API_KEY: ""
      AI_GATEWAY_API_KEY: ""
      OPENCODE_API_KEY: ""
      COPILOT_GITHUB_TOKEN: ""
      HF_TOKEN: ""
      GOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDENTIALS: ""
      GOOGLE_CLOUD_PROJECT: ""
      GCLOUD_PROJECT: ""
      GOOGLE_CLOUD_LOCATION: ""
      AWS_PROFILE: ""
      AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID: ""
      AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY: ""
      AWS_SESSION_TOKEN: ""
      AWS_REGION: ""
      AWS_DEFAULT_REGION: ""
      AWS_BEARER_TOKEN_BEDROCK: ""
      AWS_CONTAINER_CREDENTIALS_RELATIVE_URI: ""
      AWS_CONTAINER_CREDENTIALS_FULL_URI: ""
      AWS_WEB_IDENTITY_TOKEN_FILE: ""
      AZURE_OPENAI_API_KEY: ""
      AZURE_OPENAI_BASE_URL: ""
      AZURE_OPENAI_RESOURCE_NAME: ""
      PI_NO_LOCAL_LLM: "1"
    steps:
      - name: Checkout pi-mono fork
        uses: actions/checkout@v6
        with:
          path: pi-mono-fork
          fetch-depth: 0

      - name: Setup Node.js
        uses: actions/setup-node@v6
        with:
          node-version: '24'
          registry-url: 'https://npm.pkg.github.com'
          cache: npm
          cache-dependency-path: pi-mono-fork/package-lock.json

      - name: Install system dependencies
        run: sudo apt-get update && sudo apt-get install -y libcairo2-dev libpango1.0-dev libjpeg-dev libgif-dev librsvg2-dev fd-find ripgrep && sudo ln -s "$(which fdfind)" /usr/local/bin/fd

      - name: Install pi-mono dependencies
        working-directory: pi-mono-fork
        run: npm ci --ignore-scripts

      - name: Build packages
        working-directory: pi-mono-fork
        run: npm --prefix packages/tui run build && npm --prefix packages/ai run build && npm --prefix packages/agent run build && npm --prefix packages/coding-agent run build:ts

      - name: Release gate
        working-directory: pi-mono-fork
        run: npm run test:system-prompt && npm run test:cache-stability && npm run test:e2e

      - name: Fork canonical check
        working-directory: pi-mono-fork
        run: npm run check

      - name: Version or publish packages
        id: changesets
        uses: changesets/action@v1
        with:
          cwd: pi-mono-fork
          version: npm run version-packages
          publish: npm run publish:changesets
          commit: "chore(release): version fork packages"
          title: "chore(release): version fork packages"
          # We cut GitHub Releases ourselves (next step) with a bounded body.
          # The package CHANGELOG.md files are upstream-owned Keep-a-Changelog
          # (`## [x.y.z] - date`, 400KB+); the action can't match those headings
          # to the version, so it dumps the whole file as the Release body and
          # 422s past GitHub's 125000-char cap. See create-github-releases.mjs.
          createGithubReleases: false
        env:
          GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
          NODE_AUTH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}

      # Cut a GitHub Release per just-published package, with a small body that
      # points at FORK-CHANGELOG.md (never the 400KB upstream changelog), so a
      # Release is always created and publish never reds on changelog size.
      - name: Create GitHub Releases (bounded body)
        if: steps.changesets.outputs.published == 'true'
        working-directory: pi-mono-fork
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
        run: node .github/scripts/create-github-releases.mjs '${{ steps.changesets.outputs.publishedPackages }}'

#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail

# Shared auto-compaction threshold for agent harnesses.
if [ -f "$HOME/.pi/agent/token-budget.env" ]; then
  set +u
  . "$HOME/.pi/agent/token-budget.env"
  set -u
  export PI_AUTO_COMPACT_TOKEN_LIMIT CLAUDE_CODE_AUTO_COMPACT_WINDOW
fi

# Source ~/.zshenv to inherit user env (PATH, DREAM_QMD_HTTP_PORT, etc.)
# Warp launches commands via `zsh --no_rcs` which skips all rc files, so Pi
# would otherwise inherit a near-empty environment.
#
# Skip-on-sentinel: when PI_ENV_LOADED=1 is already set, the parent shell
# (or an earlier pi launch in the same shell tree) already sourced it. This
# saves ~60ms on every nested pi launch (intercom-spawned sessions, agent
# subprocesses). Warp/first-launch still pays the cost.
if [ -f "$HOME/.zshenv" ] && [ -z "${PI_ENV_LOADED:-}" ]; then
  set +u
  source "$HOME/.zshenv" 2>/dev/null || true
  set -u
  export PI_ENV_LOADED=1
fi

exec /Users/luke/Projects/personal/pi-mono-fork/packages/coding-agent/dist/pi "$@"
